items.title: JoyNews launches Tip-off initiative to amplify public concerns and expose wrongdoing
items.description: The Multimedia Group Limited’s JoyNews has launched a new initiative, JoyNews Tip-Off, to receive information from the public for investigative journalism and news reporting. The initiative is designed to provide a platform for people with information on issues of public interest to share them with the newsroom for further investigation and possible publication. Explaining the initiative, JoyNews investigative journalist Manasseh Azure said the decision was informed by the need to create an accessible channel for people who have information but may not know how to bring it to the attention of the media. He assured potential sources that JoyNews would take steps to protect their identities and ensure they are not compromised. Members of the public with information they believe deserves investigation or public attention can contact JoyNews Tip-Off via WhatsApp on 0257934478 or email joynewstipoff@myjoyonline.com . JoyNews is encouraging the public to use the platform to share credible information that could help uncover wrongdoing, promote accountability and bring important issues to public attention.

items.title: Russia–Africa Summit – Ghana must count the cost of a deeper partnership
items.description: As Moscow courts African governments with promises of trade, investment and security cooperation, Accra must guard against opaque deals, resource dependence and commercial relationships that leave the country carrying more risk than reward.Ghana’s growing economic engagement with Russia presents an opportunity, but one that demands considerably more scrutiny than diplomatic declarations of friendship and mutually beneficial cooperation might suggest. Recorded bilateral merchandise trade reached US$506.5 million in 2025, according to a compilation based on UN Comtrade data. Yet Ghana exported just US$44.9 million worth of goods to Russia, compared with imports of US$461.7 million, leaving a merchandise trade deficit of approximately US$416.8 million.The imbalance raises an uncomfortable question at the ongoing Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow on October 28 and 29: is Ghana building a relationship that will strengthen its productive capacity, or one that risks entrenching its position as a buyer of foreign goods while struggling to expand its own exports? Deeper trade is not necessarily better trade, and a growing number of bilateral agreements does not automatically translate into economic transformation. Without clear safeguards, Ghana could find itself importing more, exporting relatively little and assuming commercial or strategic obligations whose long-term costs exceed their immediate benefits.The summit should therefore be approached with commercial discipline, not diplomatic enthusiasm alone. An imbalance that demands attention Russia’s trade with Africa reportedly reached US$27.7 billion in 2025, according to figures attributed to the Russian Academy of Sciences’ Institute for African Studies. Moscow is seeking to expand its commercial footprint through agriculture, fertilisers, energy, mining, manufacturing and technology. For Ghana, there are legitimate opportunities in these areas. Reliable access to fertilisers and industrial inputs can support production, while investment in processing and manufacturing could help diversify exports and create employment. But the current structure of bilateral trade reveals a relationship in which Ghana’s export presence remains comparatively small.In the 2025 UN Comtrade-based compilation, Russian shipments to Ghana included approximately US$337 million in mineral fuels and oils and US$63 million in fertilisers. Ghana’s recorded exports were concentrated in oilseeds and other plant products, worth about US$33.5 million, cocoa products at US$6.2 million, and fats and oils at US$4.9 million. These imports may serve legitimate economic needs. The concern is whether Ghana can turn them into the basis for a more productive domestic economy, or whether the relationship will simply reinforce an existing dependence on imported goods.There is also a data question that policymakers should resolve. The Ghana News Agency reported in July that bilateral trade had risen from US$247 million in 2022 to more than US$800 million in 2024, citing the Russian ambassador. That figure differs from the 2025 customs-based compilation. The discrepancy may reflect different reporting methods or coverage, but it underlines the need for a consistent official series before the government makes ambitious claims about the relationship’s growth.A partnership cannot be evaluated properly when its underlying numbers are not readily reconciled. The danger of paying too much for strategic friendship Ghana should be particularly cautious where commercial agreements intersect with security assistance and strategic interests.In the Central African Republic and Sudan, investigations into companies linked to the Wagner Group have raised concerns about opaque gold and diamond operations and the relationship between Russian security networks and resource extraction. US authorities sanctioned several Wagner-linked entities over alleged illicit commercial activities, including gold dealings in the Central African Republic. Mali offers a different warning. Russian security assistance has expanded under the military-led government, yet the continued threat from armed groups and allegations of abuses by Russian-linked personnel have raised questions about the results delivered by the partnership.These cases do not establish that Ghana is negotiating similar arrangements. Nor do they mean that every Russian company or investment carries the same risks. They do, however, demonstrate why governments should not treat security assistance, commercial investment and diplomatic support as interchangeable benefits whose value can be assumed rather than measured. Where security and business interests overlap, governments must establish precisely what each party is providing, what it receives in return, and whether the terms serve the public interest.For Ghana, that means resisting any arrangement in which access to strategic assets, preferential concessions or long-term financial obligations is granted without transparent valuation, independent scrutiny and enforceable safeguards. The danger is not limited to outright corruption. A legally signed agreement can still be commercially disadvantageous if the state underestimates its fiscal obligations, overvalues the assistance received or fails to account for the opportunity cost of the resources committed. Sanctions and the cost of commercial exposure The geopolitical environment adds another layer of risk. Russia’s war against Ukraine and the sanctions imposed in response have complicated some transactions involving Russian counterparties. Depending on the parties and activities involved, businesses may face restrictions affecting payments, correspondent banking, shipping, insurance and access to particular markets.Ghanaian firms pursuing opportunities in Russia must therefore undertake careful due diligence on their counterparties, financing arrangements and contractual obligations. Transactions must comply with applicable sanctions and other legal requirements, while payment mechanisms should be demonstrably reliable. This is not an argument for excluding Russian businesses. It is an argument against assuming that every commercially attractive offer is necessarily executable or that the political relationship will shield Ghanaian companies from the consequences of a transaction that encounters legal or financial obstacles. The government should also avoid creating new dependencies in essential supplies. Russian fertilisers, fuel and other commodities can be useful components of Ghana’s import mix, but reliance on a narrow range of suppliers exposes domestic producers to geopolitical disruption, shipping difficulties and price volatility. Diversification is not a rejection of Russia. It is insurance against uncertainty. Investment must mean more than importing equipment The strongest argument for deeper relations with Russia would be the prospect of investment that expands Ghana’s domestic productive capacity. That is also where the government should be most demanding.Agriculture, agro-processing, fertiliser distribution and blending, energy infrastructure, manufacturing and technology offer potential areas of cooperation. But a shipment of machinery is not the same as the establishment of an industrial facility, and an investment memorandum is not evidence that capital has been committed. Proposed projects should be assessed against their financing costs, expected employment, local procurement, technology transfer, export potential and fiscal implications. Where public guarantees or other contingent liabilities are involved, those exposures should be disclosed and independently evaluated.Mining agreements require comparable scrutiny. The country should know who ultimately owns a concession, how production and exports will be verified, what taxes and royalties are due, and how environmental obligations will be enforced. These standards should apply to Russian investors just as they apply to companies from China, Europe, the United States or elsewhere. The objective is to secure investment on terms that benefit Ghana, not to confer special treatment on a foreign partner because of its geopolitical importance. The risk of confusing diplomacy with delivery The Moscow summit will generate declarations, meetings and potentially a package of agreements under the wider Russia–Africa Partnership Forum framework.But Ghana should resist the temptation to count signed documents as economic achievements before their substance has been established.Every significant agreement should have a clear implementing agency, financing arrangements, a realistic timetable and measurable targets. Progress should be reported publicly, with responsibility assigned for resolving delays or failures. The government should also assess what Ghana is committing in return. An agreement that attracts foreign investment but grants excessive tax concessions, weakens regulatory control or creates expensive future obligations may deliver less than its headline value suggests.The appropriate measure is the net economic benefit after financing costs, incentives, risks and public obligations have been considered. A more demanding partnership President John Dramani Mahama has said Ghana welcomes investment from all countries and seeks arrangements that deliver fair returns to both parties. That approach is consistent with a foreign policy that avoids exclusive geopolitical alignment.But non-alignment is most valuable when it gives a country the capacity to negotiate firmly with every partner. It loses practical meaning if the pursuit of diplomatic relationships takes precedence over commercial discipline or the protection of national interests. Ghana should therefore enter the Moscow summit with a clear set of priorities: better access for Ghanaian exports, productive investment rather than import dependence, transparent contracts, sustainable financing, technology transfer and safeguards against deceptive recruitment and other forms of exploitation.It should also insist on reliable data against which the results of the relationship can be judged. Without a consistent trade and investment baseline, it will be difficult to distinguish genuine progress from diplomatic optimism.Russia may offer useful markets, capital and expertise. But those opportunities must be evaluated against their actual returns, not the expectations surrounding them. The greatest danger is not that Ghana will engage Russia. It is that the country could deepen that engagement without adequately assessing what it stands to gain, what it may have to surrender and who will bear the cost if the promised benefits fail to materialise.The Moscow summit should be an opportunity to negotiate better terms, not a reason to suspend scrutiny. For Ghana, the test of partnership is not the scale of its diplomatic warmth but whether the relationship strengthens the economy, protects national interests and delivers measurable benefits to its citizens. >>>Ahmed Tahiru is a financial intelligence strategist, writer and advocate for financial literacy, startups, and SME growth. He is a financial strategist who believes in building businesses through systems, structures, and frameworks. He studies the startup ecosystem with a focus on creating scalable, high-impact ventures. Ahmed aspires to become a global entrepreneur, building businesses that showcase African innovation and drive the continent’s economic growth to the next level. items.title: Secret to country's development lies in AI and digitisation, PM Shehbaz stresses
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Wednesday stressed that artificial intelligence (AI) and digitalisation could improve Pakistan’s trade, exports and other areas of development and called for effective implementation of the government’s strategic partnership with global marketing company Alibaba. The premier was chairing a meeting in Islamabad reviewing progress on the use of AI and digitalisation in the economy and governance, as well as cooperation with Alibaba in these areas, according to a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO). “The secret to Pakistan’s development lies in artificial intelligence and digitalisation,” the PMO quoted him as saying. During the meeting, he said the effective use of digitalisation, AI and modern technology could play a “vital role in improving trade, exports, agricultural productivity, ease of doing business and the quality of public services in Pakistan”, PMO said. PM Shehbaz welcomed Alibaba’s cooperation in facilitating Pakistani agricultural exports to Chinese markets, highlighting that modernising the agricultural sector was essential for national development. He also welcomed cooperation with Alibaba on automation in agriculture. The prime minister directed that an AI-assisted cancer early-detection system be implemented at the earliest in collaboration with Alibaba. He also directed that a 15-day AI training programme for IT graduates be launched soon under the IT ministry’s Ignite programme, in collaboration with Alibaba. The Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) was directed to introduce an analytics system for monitoring the petroleum products supply chain in collaboration with Alibaba. The Export Promotion Board was also instructed to work with Alibaba to help increase Pakistan’s exports. The prime minister recalled that a memorandum of understanding had been signed with Alibaba at the company’s headquarters in Hangzhou during his visit to China. He said the government’s top priorities included making full use of its strategic partnership with the global company to improve small and medium enterprises’ (SMEs) access to global markets and create new opportunities for technology-driven development in the country. The prime minister directed all relevant authorities to ensure that cooperation with Alibaba was translated into tangible results through clearly defined targets, timelines and effective monitoring of all projects. He instructed the relevant ministries to complete all necessary measures by November and submit a progress report. The meeting was also briefed on progress in various sectors under the strategic cooperation between Alibaba and the Pakistan government, according to the statement. It was informed that work was under way on AI-based models for agriculture, track-and-trace technology for tobacco, and digital platforms to facilitate the export of citrus fruits and olives. A dedicated Pakistan pavilion has also been established on Alibaba’s platform to promote Pakistani products in international markets, the PMO added. A system for the digital verification of trade documents through Pakistan Single Window has been made operational. Meanwhile, a two-year programme is being launched through collaboration between the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (Smeda) and Alibaba to provide SMEs with access to international markets, training and e-commerce opportunities. The meeting also reviewed progress on developing an advanced data platform and a central data hub for the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) and Pakistan Revenue Automation Limited (PRAL), as well as a proposed pilot project for AI-assisted cancer diagnosis. In the energy sector, Ogra is being provided with AI and business intelligence tools to analyse fuel supply chain data, according to the PMO. Initiatives involving the use of digital technology and AI in higher education, railways, postal services and urban administration are also “in the final stages of completion”, the statement added. Federal ministers Ahsan Iqbal, Rana Tanveer Hussain, Jam Kamal Khan, Dr Musadik Malik, Ahad Khan Cheema, Muhammad Aurangzeb, Attaullah Tarar, Shaza Fatima Khawaja, Syed Mustafa Kamal and Abdul Aleem Khan attended the meeting, along with Minister of State Bilal Azhar Kayani and relevant senior officials. During the premier’s four-day visit to China in May this year, Pakistan expressed its support for “China’s initiative of establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation (WAICO), believing that this represents a concrete step toward promoting the development of artificial intelligence for good and for all”. In July, Pakistan became a founding member of WAICO after Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar signed the agreement establishing the forum in Shanghai, China. Earlier this year, PM Shehbaz announced the government’s plan to invest $1 billion in AI by 2030.

items.title: Filing your tax return on IRIS: A step-by-step guide for the salaried individual
items.description: Most of us feel a small knot in the stomach when someone mentions a “tax return”. We picture stacks of paper, a consultant’s fee, and a long queue at a tax office. The good news is that none of that is needed any more. If you are a salaried person, you can file your return yourself, from home, on the Federal Board of Revenue’s (FBR) online portal, IRIS. It is free and with your papers in hand it usually takes under an hour. This guide walks you through it, one click at a time. For Tax Year 2026, the last date to file is Oct 31. Why should I bother filing at all? Think of your tax return as the yearly hisaab (account) you settle at your neighbourhood shop. All year, your employer has been paying tax on your behalf every month, just like items going onto a shop’s khata (record). The return is the day you sit down with the shopkeeper, match the totals and sign off. If the shop owes you, you get it back. If you owe a little, you clear it. Either way, the book is closed and you walk away with a clean slate. Once your hisaab is settled, your name goes onto the FBR’s “Active Taxpayers List” (ATL). That is what people mean when they say someone is a “filer”. Being a filer matters in everyday life. Non-filers pay noticeably higher tax on things like bank transactions, buying a car or property, and other big-ticket dealings. And being late has become expensive. From this year, an individual who misses the deadline must pay a surcharge of Rs 25,000 to get back onto the ATL. Until last year it was Rs 1,000. Do I need to file? You should file if any of these apply to you for the year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026: Your salary was more than Rs600,000 for the year (Rs50,000 a month). You own a car with an engine capacity above 1,000cc, or own a plot or house of 500 square yards or more, or a flat in a city. You earned rent, profit on savings, dividends or business income. You want to enjoy filer rates on banking, property or vehicle deals. A common misunderstanding that comes up every tax season is the following: “My employer already cuts tax from my salary, so I’m covered.” You are not. Your employer pays the tax, but only you can file the return. Without it, you will not appear on the ATL. A simple rule of thumb: if in doubt, file. Even if you owe nothing, a return showing zero tax still makes you a filer. What does ‘Tax Year 2026’ mean? This one confuses almost everyone. Tax Year 2026 simply means the income you earned from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. It is named after the year in which it ends. So the return you are filing now, in October 2026, is for the salary you received over the last financial year. What do I need before I start? Keep these ready before you open the website. IRIS can be slow during the filing season, so the less you have to hunt for midway, the better. Your Computerised National Identity Card (CNIC) A mobile number registered in your own name, and an email address you can open. Your salary certificate (also called the annual tax deduction certificate) from your employer. It shows your total salary and the total tax deducted for the year. Ask your HR or accounts department. Tax deducted on other things, such as your mobile phone bills, electricity bills, car token tax, and profit on bank savings. Your bank can give you a withholding tax certificate. A list of what you own and what you owe on June 30, 2026: property, car, cash at home, bank balances, gold, any loans. Rough figures for your household expenses for the year: rent, utilities, school fees, travel and so on. Last year’s return, if you filed one. It makes the wealth statement much easier. Tip: write all these figures down in a notebook or a simple spreadsheet first. Typing them into IRIS from a ready sheet is quick and stress-free. Step 1: How do I register if this is my first time? If you have filed before, skip to Step 2. Go to iris.fbr.gov.pk . Click “Registration for Unregistered Person”. Enter your CNIC (without dashes), your name, your mobile number and your email address. Use a SIM that is registered against your own CNIC; shared or relatives’ numbers are a common cause of trouble. FBR will send you two one-time codes: one by SMS and one by email. Enter both. You will then receive your login password, again by SMS and email. Log in using your CNIC as the user name. You will be asked to fill a short registration form (called Form 181) with your address and source of income. If you are salaried, you will need your employer’s name and National Tax Number (NTN), which Human Resources can give you. Submit it. Once accepted, your CNIC number becomes your NTN number. Step 2: How do I open the return form? Log in at iris.fbr.gov.pk with your CNIC and password. From the top menu, click “Declaration”, then choose the income tax return. Select the period 2026. If most of your income comes from salary (more than half), choose Form 114(I). This is the simplified return made for salaried people, and it is by far the easiest. Your personal details will already be filled in from your registration. Just check them. Step 3: How do I enter my salary? Take out your salary certificate. You need two numbers from it: Total salary for the year. Total tax deducted by your employer. Enter them in the salary section exactly as they appear. Do not round off and do not estimate. The figures should match what your employer has reported to FBR. Step 4: How do I claim the tax I have already paid elsewhere? Throughout the year, small amounts of tax were also taken from you in other places. These are called “withholding taxes” and many of them can be “adjusted”, meaning they count towards your total bill. Common ones include tax on: mobile phone bills electricity bills car token tax IRIS often fills some of these in automatically. Check each figure against your bills and certificates, and add anything that is missing. Going back to our shop: this is like reminding the shopkeeper of the payments you already made on the side. They belong in the hisaab . Step 5: What is the wealth statement and how do I fill it? The wealth statement is a snapshot of what you owned and what you owed on 30 June 2026. You list your: Assets: house or plot, car, bank balances, cash in hand, gold and jewellery, investments. Liabilities: home loan, car loan, money borrowed from someone. Personal expenses for the year: rent, utilities, school fees, travel, and so on. Here is the part that confuses people. IRIS checks that your story adds up. What you owned last year + what you earned this year − what you spent = what you own this year. If these do not match, IRIS shows an “unreconciled amount”. It must come to zero before you can submit. This is the shopkeeper’s khata again. The opening balance, plus what came in, minus what went out, must equal the closing balance. If it does not, usually an expense or an asset is missing or mistyped. Go back, check your figures, and adjust honestly. Be truthful here. Penalties for hiding assets or giving misleading information have been raised sharply this year. Declaring what you own is your protection, not a risk. Step 6: How do I know if I owe anything? Click “Calculate”. IRIS will work out your tax and compare it with what has already been paid. You will see one of three results: Zero: your employer has paid exactly the right amount. This is the most common outcome for salaried people. Refundable: you have paid more than you owed. You may claim this back. Payable: you owe a little more. For a sense of scale, here is roughly what a salaried person owes for Tax Year 2026: Monthly salary Yearly salary Yearly tax Rs 50,000 Rs 600,000 Nil Rs 100,000 Rs 1,200,000 Rs 6,000 Rs 200,000 Rs 2,400,000 Rs 162,000 If your employer has been deducting tax properly, most of this will already be paid. Step 7: How do I pay if there is a balance? In IRIS, create a payment slip for income tax. This generates a PSID, a payment slip ID number. Pay that PSID through your bank’s mobile app, internet banking or at a branch. Once paid, you get a CPR (Computerised Payment Receipt) number. Enter the CPR number in your return so IRIS knows the tax has been paid. Step 8: How do I submit? Check the unreconciled amount once more. It must be zero. Click “Submit”. Enter the PIN you created when you first registered. IRIS will issue an acknowledgement slip. Download it and keep it safe, along with a copy of your return. This is your proof of filing. Congratulations. Your hisaab is closed for the year. Step 9: How do I check that I am now a filer? Once the ATL is updated, you can check your status in two easy ways: By SMS: type ATL, a space, then your 13-digit CNIC, and send it to 9966. Online: search your CNIC on the ATL section of FBR’s website. What if IRIS is slow or keeps giving errors? You will not be alone. IRIS has been sluggish this season, especially close to the deadline. File early. Do not wait for the final day. Try during quiet hours, early morning or late at night. Click “Save” often. The auto-save feature has been removed this year, so an unsaved page can be lost. Keep your figures on paper or in a spreadsheet, so re-entering them is quick if something goes wrong. If an error message makes no sense, take a screenshot and contact the FBR’s helpline or a tax practitioner. Myths vs reality Myth: “My employer deducts tax, so I don’t need to file.” Reality: Your employer pays the tax. Only you can file the return. Myth: “My income is too low to bother.” Reality: Filing a return showing zero tax still makes you a filer, and that saves you money elsewhere. Myth: “If I declare my car or plot, I’ll get a notice.” Reality: It is hiding assets that gets you into trouble, and penalties for that have gone up. Myth: “I need to pay a consultant.” Reality: Not for a simple salaried return. This guide is all you need. When should I get professional help? You can do a simple salaried return yourself. Consider a tax practitioner if you have: A business or freelance income More than one property or rental income Sold property or shares during the year Income or assets abroad The bottom line Filing your return is not a favour to the government. It is a small, once-a-year chore that keeps your own finances clean and saves you real money on the big purchases of life: a car, a home, your children’s future. Gather your papers, set aside an evening, and settle your hisaab . Do it before Oct 31, and do it once properly. Next year, it will take you half the time. Dates and rules quoted are as announced by FBR at the time of writing. Please check iris.fbr.gov.pk or FBR’s announcements for any further changes before you file.

items.title: Cœlioscopie au CHU Donka : une troisième mission pour consolider les acquis
items.description: Le Centre hospitalier universitaire (CHU) Donka accueille une troisième mission de formation et de soins en cœlioscopie, menée en collaboration avec une équipe médicale française. Elle vise à approfondir les compétences pratiques des chirurgiens guinéens tout en assurant la prise en charge de patients présentant différentes pathologies abdominales et gynécologiques. 23 patients concernés par cette troisième mission Le nombre de patients concernés par les missions successives est en progression : 6 lors de la première, 13 lors de la deuxième et 23 pour cette troisième édition. Pour le Pr Fodé Lansana Camara, chef du service de chirurgie viscérale, cette évolution témoigne de l’intérêt croissant de la population pour cette technique chirurgicale. Les pathologies prises en charge comprennent notamment les hernies de la paroi abdominale, l’appendicite, les kystes ovariens, les obstructions des trompes et certaines affections de la vésicule biliaire. Un transfert progressif des compétences Cette troisième mission s’inscrit dans la continuité des deux précédentes, avec un accent particulier sur le perfectionnement des gestes techniques. Selon le Pr Fodé Lansana Camara, les missions antérieures ont permis aux chirurgiens guinéens de progresser dans la pratique de la cœlioscopie et de réaliser désormais certains gestes de manière autonome « Cette mission a contribué à améliorer de façon significative et progressive la main des chirurgiens guinéens. Il faut le reconnaître, notamment les open – coelio s , certains gestes comme la dépariétalisation lors des herniorraphie … que nous les faisons nous-mêmes désormais . Donc, nous remercions vraiment nos formateurs à cette occasion et nous suggérons la continuité de cette mission. » a fait savoir le Pr Lansana CAMARA. Jean-Philippe Combier , chirurgien viscéral français spécialisé en chirurgie digestive et gynécologique, souligne la motivation des praticiens guinéens et la qualité de la collaboration. Il estime que la poursuite de ces échanges permettra à l’équipe locale de renforcer ses compétences et de gagner progressivement en autonomie. Jean-Philippe Combier évoque la possibilité d’organiser deux missions par an afin de poursuivre l’accompagnement des chirurgiens guinéens. À terme, l’objectif est de leur permettre de maîtriser davantage la cœlioscopie et de poursuivre cette pratique de façon autonome. Le CHU Donka salue l’accompagnement des formateurs et souhaite la poursuite de cette coopération médicale . Pour Mamadou Aliou BAH Administrateur Général par intérim de l’hôpital, le développement des pratiques chirurgicales fait partie des objectifs clés de la concession canadienne afin de relever le niveau du CHU et réduire les évacuations sanitaires. « La Coelioscopie permet de réduire la durée de l’hospitalisation du patient qui peut rentrer à domicile seulement 24 heures après l’intervention sans oublier que le patient ne subit pas une grosse incision ce qui a pour avantage d’éviter de grosses cicatrices. Le développement de cette chirurgie au sein du CHU Donka fait donc partie de notre stratégie globale de modernisation des soins et de développement des capacités de nos chirurgiens » a laissé entendre l’administrateur Général par intérim. L’article Cœlioscopie au CHU Donka : une troisième mission pour consolider les acquis est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: 2027: ‘We’ll rig those who rig elections,’ Peter Obi talks tough
items.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has threatened to deal with those who rig elections in Nigeria, declaring that his administration would ensure electoral offenders face jail terms if he wins the 2027 presidential election. Obi spoke on Wednesday at an NDC town hall meeting in Nasarawa State, where he addressed party supporters on electoral integrity and the need to strengthen Nigeria’s electoral system. Responding to a question about election rigging, the former Anambra State governor said the party would not allow electoral manipulation to go unchallenged in the next general election. “You didn’t ask about what we are going to do if people rig election next year. Let me assure you, number one, this coming election, we will rig those who rig it,” Obi said. He added that, if elected president, he would ensure that election rigging became impossible under his watch by strengthening political parties and reforming the electoral process. “And let me assure you number two, if I’m elected the President of Nigeria, nobody will rig election in this country again because the first thing we need to do is to strengthen our parties, strengthen the process,” he said. Obi also called for stricter laws governing eligibility to contest elections, arguing that candidates should be required to demonstrate that they had attended primary and secondary school. “Our laws will be strict. For you to contest election, you must have attended a primary school, you must have attended a secondary school and it will be visible, it will be clear,” he said. He warned that anyone who forged academic certificates or falsely claimed to possess the required qualifications would face imprisonment. “If you didn’t attend any of them or forge your certificate, you go to jail,” Obi said. The NDC candidate extended the warning to officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and others involved in election administration, saying anyone found guilty of rigging elections under his government would be prosecuted. “Any INEC official, anybody who is involved with elections under my watch that rigs elections will go to jail,” he declared. Obi said his proposed approach would be anchored on the rule of law, insisting that no individual, regardless of position, should be exempt from accountability. “Under my watch, Nigeria must be a country that has a law, and both from the number one person to the last person must obey the rule of law,” he said. “Nobody must be above the law; nobody will behave rascally.” He said his political ambition was driven by a desire to change the country and build a system in which electoral rules were respected. “That’s why we are doing what we are doing. We want to change Nigeria. A new Nigeria is possible, and that new Nigeria will be OK,” Obi added. items.title: El “espectáculo inmoral de la feria de oportunidades de Franco” revienta las expectativas de recaudación
items.description: El mayor éxito artístico para Isabel de Cubas, cuñada de Carmen Franco aficionada a pintar, llegó insospechadamente 18 años después de su muerte en 2008. La esposa de Andrés Martínez-Bordiú, conde de Morata de Jalón y hermano del marqués de Villaverde, reventó todos los pronósticos en la primera sesión de la subasta de suvenires del pazo de Meirás que se celebra esta semana en Madrid, cuando su pequeño cuadro —tasado por las expertas de Magna Art Auctions en 50 euros— desató la locura entre los postores. De un soplido, el óleo naíf (que representa toscamente la fachada del pazo que disfrutò la familia del dictador ocho décadas) disparó su cotización hasta los 6.000 euros . Para los nostálgicos, o fanáticos, esta pintura sobre tabla era importante pese a su técnica elemental; no solo por su temática, sino porque la autora había incluido por la parte trasera una dedicatoria: “Para mi querida Carmen Franco, con todo mi cariño”. items.title: Burkina: un individu «se ferait passer pour un agent de l’ONEA»
items.description: L'Office National de l’Eau et de l’Assainissement (ONEA), dans un communiqué, ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026, appelle sa clientèle à la vigilance, après la diffusion d’ «une publication montrant une personne portant une tenue bleue marquée « ONAB » qui se ferait passer, depuis un certain temps, pour un agent de l’ONEA auprès des populations». «L'Office National de l’Eau et de l’Assainissement (ONEA) a été alerté par une publication montrant une personne portant une tenue bleue marquée « ONAB » qui se ferait passer, depuis un certain temps, pour un agent de l’ONEA auprès des populations. Face à cette situation, l’ONEA invite l’ensemble de ses abonnés et la population à faire preuve de vigilance tout en facilitant les interventions des agents assermentés de l'ONEA qui doivent faire leur travail afin d'assurer la continuité du service. Pour reconnaître un agent de l’ONEA, voici quelques éléments d’identification : – La tenue professionnelle : les agents portent une tenue de couleur bleue, marquée du logo ONEA qui est différent du logo porté sur la tenue du prétendu releveur qui porte la mention (ONAB). – Le badge professionnel des agents permanents qui comporte notamment une photographie permettant d’identifier son titulaire. – Le badge des agents contractuels : il porte la mention « Contractuel », un numéro de badge ainsi que l’indication de l’agence de rattachement de l'agent. L’ONEA recommande à ses abonnés de ne pas hésiter à vérifier l’identité de toute personne intervenant à leur domicile ou dans leur quartier au nom de l’Office. En cas de doute ou de comportement suspect, les populations sont invitées à contacter les services compétents de l’ONEA au 80 00 11 11 par appels ou sur notre Whatsapp au 52 20 20 85. L'ONEA compte sur la vigilance et l'accompagnement de tous pour la délivrance de ses services dans les meilleures conditions.» ONEA, votre bien-être, notre raison d’être ! items.title: From windfall to wealth: how to make your money last
items.description: Receiving a financial windfall, whether through an inheritance, gift from family or prize winnings can fast-track major financial goals and responsibilities. However, without a clear plan, a sudden windfall can easily become a missed opportunity to building long lasting wealth. As more young people focus on financial independence and long-term wealth creation, young adults are encouraged to view a financial windfall not as spending money, but as a foundation for future financial security. Akweley Laryea, Head of Retail Banking at First National Bank shared that one of the biggest mistakes young adults make is treating a windfall as an opportunity to immediately upgrade their lifestyle. “Many young people dream of owning a home, driving a new car or travelling the world. While a financial windfall may make these goals achievable immediately, it is important to first define your financial goals. The decisions made in the first few months can have a significant impact on future financial wellbeing,” adds Akweley as she shares financial considerations to take into account: Don’t make major financial decisions immediately: Take time to develop a structured financial plan that considers your short, medium to long term financial needs so that you avoid unnecessary spending. Seek professional advice: we encourage young people to avoid making significant financial commitments for at least six to 12 months after receiving a windfall. This provides time to seek advice, gain a full understanding of their financial needs and make decisions that support long-term wealth creation rather than short-term gratification. Set clear financial goals: a financial windfall can create significant opportunities, but managing it wisely is important. Young adults should focus on setting clear financial goals, reducing costly debt, building an emergency fund and invest for long-term growth. Make informed decisions: young people are also encouraged to avoid rushing into business ventures or investment opportunities. It is advisable to rather take the time to understand these opportunities fully and obtain appropriate advice before committing funds. Don’t resign from your job: be cautious of viewing a windfall as a replacement for employment or career growth. A financial windfall should complement and not replace your career ambitions. Continuing to work, building skills and enhancing your earning potential remains one of the most effective ways to preserve and grow wealth over time. Giving a gift that creates wealth: Financial windfalls do not always arrive through inheritances or prize winnings. Increasingly, families are looking for meaningful ways to transfer wealth and create financial opportunities for loved ones during important milestones. What if those moments became opportunities to build wealth instead? This is where innovative solutions such as the FNB Investment Gift Card are changing the way people think about gifting. Instead of giving cash that may quickly be spent, families and friends can gift an investment that provides the recipient with an opportunity to start or grow their wealth journey. “Whether it is helping a young graduate take their first step into investing, contributing towards a child’s future, supporting newlyweds as they build their financial future, or celebrating a professional milestone, an investment gift has the potential to create value long after the occasion has passed”. By shifting from consumption-based gifting to investment-based gifting, families can play a meaningful role in building a stronger culture of saving and investing across generations. Akweley adds that families should proactively prepare younger beneficiaries for future inheritances. We often underestimate the responsibility that comes with inheriting money. Where possible, families should start conversations early and help younger beneficiaries understand the financial responsibilities that may come with managing large amounts of money. “Receiving a financial windfall is rare. For young people, it can be a powerful opportunity to build wealth, achieve financial freedom and create a stronger financial future, provided it is managed with patience, discipline and the right support,” concludes Akweley.

items.title: Road crashes drop by 9.4% following TraffiTech sensitisation – MTTD
items.description: The Director of Education, Research and Training at the Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD), ACP Alexander Kwaku Obeng, says road crashes reported across Ghana declined by 9.4% following intensified sensitisation and caution notices issued to motorists under the TraffiTech-GH pilot project. He said the police recorded 1,003 crashes in September this year, down from 1,108 during the same period in 2025. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Wednesday, ACP Obeng attributed the reduction to increased public awareness and messages sent to vehicle owners, alerting them to traffic offences captured by the system. “Within twenty days of September this year, when we enhanced sensitisation, gathering evidence and confronting vehicle owners with it with an embedded message, with GPS, MTTD sender ID sending messages saying ‘speed kills, reduce it now’ with your vehicle number, time and place of the offence,” he said. He explained that a comparison of crash data for September 2025 and September 2026 showed a change in driver behaviour. “If you compare the data of crashes from September last year (2025) with the same period this year, we have seen a significant change in behaviour of drivers,” he added. ACP Obeng said the number of vehicles involved in crashes also fell from 1,928 in September 2025 to 1,693 this year, representing a 12.19% reduction. The number of people injured in road crashes declined by 15.02%, from 1,405 to 1,194 over the same period. TraffiTech-GH is currently being piloted and has not yet been rolled out nationwide. Traffitech-GH is an automated system developed by the Ghana Police Service to enforce road traffic laws and regulations and improve road safety in the country. The system uses cameras and sensors to automatically take a picture and or video of vehicles that flout road traffic laws and regulations, such as speeding and running a red light

items.title: Kédougou : une attaque armée dans un site minier fait un blessé grave et 6,7 millions de FCFA emportés
items.description: Des individus armés ont fait irruption dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi dans un périmètre minier de Faranding, dans le département de Saraya, région de Kédougou (sud-est). Ils auraient grièvement agressé un ressortissant chinois avant d’emporter une somme de 6,7 millions de francs CFA. Selon l’Agence de presse sénégalaise (APS), qui cite une source sécuritaire, les faits se seraient produits vers 2 heures du matin dans une base exploitée par une entreprise chinoise. Six individus armés auraient fait irruption dans les lieux, tiré des coups de feu en l’air, puis contraint le vigile en poste sur un mirador à descendre sous la menace de leurs armes. La même source a indiqué avoir entendu des appels au secours provenant du logement du personnel, où un ressortissant chinois aurait été agressé. La victime n’aurait été découverte qu’après le départ des assaillants. Présenté comme le trésorier de la base et âgé d’une quarantaine d’années, le ressortissant chinois aurait été évacué pour recevoir des soins médicaux. Les circonstances exactes de l’agression et l’ampleur du préjudice restent à établir par les investigations. D’après les premières indications rapportées par l’APS, les assaillants, dont l’identité et la destination restent inconnues, auraient emporté 6 700 000 francs CFA. Ils seraient armés de fusils et d’armes de poing. Les Forces de défense et de sécurité sont mobilisées pour effectuer les premières constatations et mener des recherches dans la zone. Une enquête est en cours afin de déterminer les circonstances précises de cette attaque et d’identifier les personnes impliquées.

items.title: Carrick, Fernandes, hold peace talks after Bournemouth neglect
items.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and head coach Michael Carrick have held private talks to resolve tensions ahead of the club’s Premier League clash with Chelsea on Saturday. The meeting followed Fernandes’ omission from the starting line-up in United’s 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth on Sunday, after the Portuguese midfielder reportedly criticised Carrick’s tactics following a 4-1 loss to Como in the Champions League. BBC Sport report that the pair met privately at United’s training ground on Tuesday to discuss their differences and clear the air before the team travels to Stamford Bridge. Fernandes, 32, remained an unused substitute against Bournemouth but could return to the starting line-up when United face Chelsea at 12:30 GMT on Saturday. Carrick, meanwhile, will remain in charge for the fixture despite mounting pressure over the team’s poor performances. The 45-year-old was widely expected to lose his job following the Bournemouth defeat, but United’s board has decided to give him another opportunity to turn the situation around. The club currently sit 16th in the Premier League table, having recorded just one victory in eight league matches this season. Despite the disappointing run, senior figures at Old Trafford reportedly believe Carrick should not bear the entire responsibility for the team’s struggles. The board is understood to consider the squad capable of qualifying for the Champions League and believes the players have failed to perform to their expected standard. In a further boost for Carrick, midfielder Kobbie Mainoo returned to training on Wednesday after spending a fortnight on the sidelines with an injury. However, uncertainty remains over Carrick’s long-term future, with United reportedly drawing up a shortlist of potential replacements. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe and ex Germany and Bayern Munich head coach Julian Nagelsmann are among the names being considered. Saturday’s encounter with Chelsea could therefore prove significant for Carrick as he attempts to improve United’s results and restore confidence within the squad. The talks with Fernandes may also help ease tensions between the manager and his captain as United seek to recover from their latest setback. items.description: Le quartier Kènèndé, dans la commune urbaine de Kindia, est en deuil après la mort tragique de Hadja Mariam, âgée d’environ 68 ans, victime d’un incendie survenu dans son domicile aux premières heures de la matinée de ce mercredi. Selon les premiers témoignages recueillis sur place, le sinistre serait lié à une installation électrique. Malgré les efforts déployés par son fils et la mobilisation des voisins, la victime n’a pas pu être sauvée. Le Commissaire principal de police en service à Mafanco, Morlaye Camara raconte avec émotion sa tentative désespérée de sauver celle qui lui a donné la vie. « Ce matin, à mon réveil, j’étais sur la véranda. Ma sœur m’a dit qu’elle voulait rentrer à la maison pour prendre mon sac et récupérer un document qui devait être photocopié. Lorsque ma mère l’a entendue, elle l’a également suivie. Pendant que j’étais toujours sur la véranda, j’ai soudainement entendu des cris. Je suis alors rentré précipitamment pour tenter de sauver ma mère. Malheureusement, je l’ai trouvée allongée dans la chambre, au milieu des flammes. J’ai essayé de la sauver, mais la situation était extrêmement difficile », témoigne-t-il, dépité. Les cris de détresse ont rapidement attiré les riverains, qui se sont mobilisés pour tenter de venir en aide à la famille. Mais en vain. Profondément éprouvés par cette disparition brutale, le mari de la défunte et sa fille n’ont pas été en mesure de témoigner, tant la douleur était vive au moment du passage de notre équipe.

YAWC Network calls for revocation of licences of teachers convicted of sexual abuse
items.description: The Executive Director of the Young African Women Congress (YAWC) Network, Daniel Osei Tuffour, has called for the revocation of the teaching licences of teachers found guilty of sexually abusing students, arguing that transferring offenders to other schools is not enough to protect children. He has urged the Ghana Education Service (GES) and other relevant authorities to impose stricter sanctions on teachers who commit sexual offences against students, including prosecution and the withdrawal of their professional licences. Mr Tuffour made the call at the YAWC Network’s 10th anniversary celebration in Accra on Monday, October 26. His comments follow a JoyNews documentary by investigative journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni that exposed allegations of sexual abuse involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School. Mr Tuffour questioned the practice of transferring teachers accused of sexual misconduct to other schools, warning that it could expose more students to abuse if appropriate disciplinary and legal action was not taken. “GES and other authorities should bring stricter sanctions. I don’t see why a teacher will molest a girl and the sanction is just to transfer them to a different school, and they will go and continue such atrocities,” he said. “Apart from being made to face the full rigours of the law, their licences must be revoked,” he added. Calls for stronger protection for victims Mr Tuffour said sexual abuse could leave victims with long-term psychological trauma and urged authorities to ensure that cases were investigated and prosecuted regardless of the perpetrators’ backgrounds or affiliations. He also expressed concern about the handling of the Obuasi Senior High Technical School case, insisting that sexual offences involving children must be treated with the seriousness they deserve. The YAWC Network executive director further attributed the reluctance of some victims to report abuse to victim-blaming attitudes and financial difficulties. He said inadequate support systems could prevent victims from speaking out, reporting offences and pursuing justice. “There are a lot of victims, but because there’s no support system, there is no support anywhere, we find them not being bold to report some of these cases,” he said. Mr Tuffour encouraged victims of sexual abuse to seek help and report their experiences, assuring them that the YAWC Network was prepared to offer support.

items.title: CRIEF : le nouveau président, Mamadou Saliou Diakité, promet fermeté et respect des principes du procès pénal
items.description: Nommé le 21 octobre dernier, le nouveau président de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF), Mamadou Saliou Diakité, a officiellement pris ses fonctions ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026. Il succède à la tête de cette juridiction au juge Francis Kova Zoumanigui, également nommé inspecteur général des services judiciaires et pénitentiaires. Dans son allocution de prise de fonctions, le magistrat a déclaré : « En prenant les rênes de cette juridiction, nous ambitionnons d’inscrire nos actions dans la pérennisation des acquis, tout en répondant aux exigences légitimes de nos concitoyens. Nous entendons particulièrement garantir aux justiciables de cette institution une justice moderne, transparente, équitable et rendue dans le strict respect du délai raisonnable. » Le nouveau président a également réaffirmé la détermination de la CRIEF à poursuivre la lutte contre les crimes économiques et financiers, tout en respectant les garanties judiciaires. « Autant nous promettons que la CRIEF demeurera debout dans la lutte contre les crimes économiques et financiers, autant nous rassurons qu’elle le fera dans le strict respect des principes sacro-saints du procès pénal », a-t-il assuré. Mamadou Saliou Diakité a, par ailleurs, souligné que la réalisation de ses ambitions dépendrait de l’implication de l’ensemble des acteurs de la juridiction. « Je reste convaincu que, quelles que soient la noblesse de mes ambitions, elles ne pourraient être atteintes que si je suis accompagné par les acteurs et auxiliaires de notre juridiction », a-t-il indiqué. Dans cette dynamique, il a tendu la main aux magistrats du siège et du parquet, aux greffiers, au personnel d’appui, aux avocats, aux huissiers et aux notaires. Il a également sollicité la collaboration des partenaires nationaux et internationaux, ainsi que l’accompagnement des autorités pour renforcer le capital humain de la Cour et améliorer ses conditions de travail. Pour conclure, le nouveau président de la CRIEF s’est dit convaincu que l’union des efforts permettra de surmonter les obstacles, de réaliser les aspirations communes et de bâtir une justice plus prospère pour les générations futures. Elisa Camara L’article CRIEF : le nouveau président, Mamadou Saliou Diakité, promet fermeté et respect des principes du procès pénal est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

Mondial U-15 : la FIFA salue les performances des Lionceaux de l’Atlas et les ambitions du football marocain
items.description: La sélection marocaine U-15 s’est illustrée lors de la première édition de la Coupe du Monde et Festival U-15 à Bakou, en Azerbaïdjan, avec cinq victoires en autant de rencontres lors de la phase préliminaire. Dans un article publié sur sa plateforme Inside FIFA, la Fédération internationale de football met en avant les performances des Lionceaux de l’Atlas et les perspectives offertes à la nouvelle génération du football marocain. Le football marocain poursuit son développement sur la scène internationale, et les jeunes talents en sont désormais l’une des vitrines. Dans un article intitulé « Maroc : les succès d’aujourd’hui, les ambitions de demain », publié sur Inside FIFA, la Fédération internationale de football (FIFA) met en lumière le parcours de la sélection nationale des moins de 15 ans (U-15) lors de la première Coupe du Monde et Festival U-15, organisée du 24 au 30 octobre à Bakou. Dirigés par Karim Miftal, les Lionceaux de l’Atlas ont remporté leurs cinq rencontres de la phase préliminaire. Un bilan qui, selon la plateforme de la FIFA, témoigne de leur capacité à s’adapter à des adversaires issus de différents horizons footballistiques. Une expérience internationale au service de la formation Au-delà des résultats, cette compétition représente une occasion pour les jeunes joueurs marocains de diversifier leur apprentissage et de se confronter à des styles de jeu différents. « C’est une très belle expérience, sur le plan humain comme sur le plan sportif », a déclaré Karim Miftal à Inside FIFA, soulignant l’intérêt de cette confrontation internationale pour le développement de ses joueurs, habituellement davantage confrontés à des équipes africaines et européennes. Le format du tournoi, disputé à huit contre huit, favorise les interactions avec le ballon, la rapidité d’exécution et la multiplication des situations de jeu. Une formule qui permet aux jeunes footballeurs de développer leurs qualités techniques et tactiques tout en évoluant dans un environnement différent de celui auquel ils sont habitués. Dans la continuité des succès du football marocain Pour Inside FIFA, les performances des U-15 s’inscrivent dans une dynamique plus large, marquée par les résultats des différentes sélections nationales marocaines ces dernières années. Le parcours historique des Lions de l’Atlas à la Coupe du Monde 2022 au Qatar, où le Maroc a atteint les demi-finales, puis le sacre des Lionceaux de l’Atlas U-20 au Mondial 2025 au Chili, ont contribué à renforcer la visibilité du football marocain à l’échelle internationale. Ces succès mettent également en lumière le potentiel des nouvelles générations et les ambitions du Royaume en matière de formation et de développement des talents. Le Maroc se projette vers les grandes compétitions internationales La FIFA évoque également les perspectives ouvertes par l’organisation de grandes compétitions internationales au Maroc. Le Royaume accueille notamment la Coupe du Monde féminine U-17 sur cinq éditions consécutives, de 2025 à 2029. Le pays prépare par ailleurs la coorganisation de la Coupe du Monde 2030 avec l’Espagne et le Portugal. Cette échéance pourrait offrir à certains jeunes joueurs actuellement en formation l’opportunité de participer à la plus grande compétition du football mondial sur leur propre sol. La première édition de la Coupe du Monde et Festival U-15 réunit à Bakou des équipes issues de 189 fédérations membres de la FIFA. Pensé comme un événement à la fois sportif et éducatif, le tournoi vise à favoriser le développement des jeunes joueurs grâce aux rencontres internationales, aux échanges entre délégations et à des activités de sensibilisation. À travers le parcours des Lionceaux de l’Atlas, la FIFA met ainsi en perspective les résultats immédiats de la sélection marocaine et les ambitions à long terme du football national. The post Mondial U-15 : la FIFA salue les performances des Lionceaux de l’Atlas et les ambitions du football marocain appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: NPP drags Mahama to Supreme Court over interpretation of 2-term limit
items.description: The New Patriotic Party (NPP) has filed a suit at the Supreme Court seeking an interpretation of the constitutional provisions governing presidential term limits, in a case that could determine whether President John Dramani Mahama is eligible to seek another term in office in 2028. The writ of summons and statement of case, dated July 28, 2026, were filed by the party’s solicitor, Godfred Yeboah Dame of Dame & Partners, with the Attorney-General named as the defendant. The party is asking the court to clarify whether the constitutional limit of two presidential terms applies regardless of whether the terms are served consecutively or are separated by a period out of office. In its statement of case, the NPP is seeking declarations on the interpretation of Articles 58(2) and 66(1), (2) and (3)(a) of the 1992 Constitution. Among other reliefs, the party wants the court to declare that the presidential term limit means a maximum of two terms, whether consecutive or non-consecutive. It is also asking the court to affirm that a person cannot be elected President more than twice and cannot hold the office for more than two four-year terms, amounting to eight years in total. The NPP is further seeking clarification on the eligibility of a Vice-President who assumes the presidency for more than half of a predecessor’s unexpired term. It wants the court to declare that such a person would be eligible to contest for election as President for only one term. The party is also asking the court to clarify whether a person who has previously served one presidential term may serve only one additional term, regardless of whether the two terms are consecutive. The suit follows public debate over whether the constitutional phrase “two terms” could be interpreted to mean two consecutive terms rather than two terms in total. The NPP argues that such an interpretation could allow a person who has served one term, lost an attempt at immediate re-election and later returned to office to serve two additional terms. The party describes that interpretation as a threat to the constitutional framework governing presidential tenure. “Plaintiff considers this proposition not only absurd but dangerous for the democracy, peace and stability of the nation,” the statement of case reads. It argues that adopting such an interpretation would effectively introduce words into the Constitution that are not contained in the text. “Acceding to this interpretation will condone and sanction manipulation of clear provisions in the Constitution as it involves inserting words into the constitutional text—it will involve amending the Constitution through judicial fiat,” the party states. The NPP’s arguments also draw on international examples, including the United States’ 22nd Amendment, which limits the number of times a person may be elected President. The party further refers to constitutional developments in other African countries and argues that attempts to alter presidential term limits have contributed to political instability in some jurisdictions. It also cites the Constitution Review Commission’s 2011 report, which recommended an amendment to clarify that a person who has served two presidential terms would not qualify to stand for re-election. items.title: John Darko calls for stronger women’s representation in Parliament
items.description: The Member of Parliament for Suame, John Darko, has called for greater representation of women in Parliament and other leadership positions, warning that their underrepresentation limits the range of perspectives shaping national decisions. Speaking at an event organised by the Young African Women Congress Network (YAWC Network) in Accra on Monday, October 26, he said Ghana was missing out on the skills, experience and ideas women could contribute to national development. “A democracy that excludes women from meaningful participation in political and economic decision-making deprives itself of the competence, experiences and perspectives of substantial portions of its citizens,” he said. Mr Darko described women’s participation in political leadership as essential to an effective and representative democracy. He noted that although women make up approximately half of Ghana’s population, their representation in Parliament remains disproportionately low. “Ghana’s Parliament presently comprises 276 members, of whom only 41 are women. Women constitute approximately half of our population, yet their presence in the principal institution responsible for making laws, approving national expenditure and scrutinising our executive authority remains disproportionately low,” he said. Representing the Minority Leader at the event, Mr Darko urged stakeholders to intensify efforts to remove barriers preventing women from participating fully in political and economic decision-making. YAWC marks 10 years of advocacy The event formed part of activities marking the tenth anniversary of the Young African Women Congress Network, which advocates greater opportunities and representation for women and girls. The network’s Global President, Dr Stephanie Wirba, said that despite progress over the past decade, many girls and women continued to face barriers to education, healthcare, employment and leadership. “We have won battles, but we have not won the war. Our girls are still out of school, our mothers are still dying in childbirth, our girls are still married before they can vote, and a woman is still asked for sex to get a job,” she said. Dr Wirba’s remarks highlighted what she described as persistent challenges facing women and girls, despite efforts to advance gender equality. Calls for stronger implementation of affirmative action The Executive Director of the Young African Women Congress, Daniel Osei Tuffuor, called on public institutions to move beyond commitments and take concrete steps to expand opportunities for women and girls. He questioned the progress made in implementing Ghana’s affirmative action legislation and urged authorities to demonstrate greater commitment to putting agreed measures into practice. “It’s been how many years now since we passed the affirmative action bill, have we been able to achieve even 20% of that? Our authorities have to be intentional about implementation these bills. Until they are intentional, we will go and come, go and come and still be at where we are,” he said. He added that public authorities had a responsibility to implement measures designed to improve women’s representation and participation. Network shifts focus towards opportunities and mentorship As it marks its tenth anniversary, the YAWC Network says it intends to place greater emphasis on securing practical opportunities for women, alongside its advocacy work. Mentorship will also be a priority over the next decade, with established members expected to support younger women seeking to enter leadership positions. The initiative is intended to help more women develop the experience, confidence and networks needed to participate in decision-making across public and private institutions.

items.title: Marché russe : la Tunisie entend valoriser le potentiel de ses exportations
items.description: Dans le contexte du rapprochement russo-africain, a l'occasion du troisieme Forum Russie-Afrique, qui se tient les 28 et 29 octobre a Moscou, la Tunisie entend promouvoir ses exportations vers le marche russe, notamment celles d'huile d'olive et de produits agroalimentaires. Selon les estimations du bureau du Centre de promotion des exportations (CEPEX) a Moscou, le potentiel commercial encore inexploite atteint 27 millions de dollars. La Russie, qui considere la securite alimentaire comme un pilier de sa cooperation avec l'Afrique, se dit ouverte aux possibilites de partenariat agricole et commercial avec les pays du continent. Dans ce contexte, l'huile d'olive tunisienne represente un important atout commercial, avec un potentiel d'exportation inexploite de 4,7 millions de dollars. Selon le CEPEX, 85 % des opportunites dans cette filiere restent « non captees ». D'autres creneaux presentent egalement un potentiel considerable, notamment les pieces automobiles, les articles d'habillement, les equipements medicaux et certains produits agroalimentaires. Au cours des neuf premiers mois de 2026, les importations tunisiennes en provenance de Russie ont recule de 54 %, s'etablissant a 1 552,3 millions de dinars (environ 517 millions de dollars), contre 3 375,1 millions de dinars (environ 1,125 milliard de dollars) durant la meme periode de 2025. Parallelement, les exportations tunisiennes vers la Russie ont progresse de 14 %, atteignant 32,4 millions de dinars (environ 10,8 millions de dollars). Cette evolution contribue a reduire le deficit commercial de la Tunisie avec la Russie. Sur l'ensemble de l'annee 2025, celui-ci s'etait etabli a 4 186,7 millions de dinars (environ 1,395 milliard de dollars), contre 5 384,4 millions de dinars (environ 1,795 milliard de dollars) en 2024. L'agroalimentaire, moteur des exportations tunisiennes vers la Russie Le secteur agroalimentaire constitue le principal moteur des exportations tunisiennes vers la Russie, representant 70 % du total. Suivent les industries diverses (13 %), le textile et l'habillement (12 %), ainsi que les industries mecaniques et electriques (5 %). Parmi les produits tunisiens les plus exportes vers la Russie figurent les dattes, qui representent 31,88 % du total, suivies de l'huile d'olive (13,62 %), des preparations et conserves de poisson (13,31 %), des bandes et lames en matieres plastiques (8,89 %), puis des costumes et ensembles vestimentaires (7,90 %). Du cote des importations, la Tunisie s'approvisionne principalement en produits petroliers russes, qui ont represente 69 % du total au cours des sept premiers mois de 2026. Viennent ensuite le ble dur (12 %), les huiles de navette ou de colza (7 %), l'orge (3 %) et les fils en aluminium (2 %), ainsi que d'autres produits, notamment le ble tendre et le meteil.

items.title: Instagram to allow creators upload videos up to 90 minutes
items.description: Instagram is testing a new feature that will allow selected creators to upload videos lasting up to 90 minutes, marking a major shift from the platform’s traditional focus on short-form content. The feature, called “Features”, will allow users to watch longer videos, including podcasts, interviews and comedy shows, directly on the Meta-owned platform without switching to other services. Instagram announced the test on Monday, with the company expanding its efforts to compete in the growing market for long-form digital video content. Instagram head Adam Mosseri, who previously opposed introducing longer videos on the platform, said the company had decided to embrace the format for several reasons. “For a long time, I have been against doing long-form video on Instagram,” Mosseri said in a video shared alongside Tessa Lyons, the company’s vice president of product. “But we are actually going to lean in for a bunch of different reasons,” he added. Lyons described the move as a new phase in Instagram’s video development, noting that the platform was beginning to explore ways of accommodating longer storytelling formats. “It feels like a full circle moment that we’re here now talking about the beginning of our journey on the long-form video,” she said. Under the new feature, users who come across short vertical clips on their feeds will be able to tap a prompt to watch the full video in a horizontal format within the app. The development is expected to make it easier for podcasters and other creators to use Instagram not only to promote their content but also to distribute complete episodes. Mosseri explained that creators currently use Instagram to attract audiences before directing them to other platforms to watch full-length videos. “You slice it up, you use platforms like Instagram as the top of the funnel to raise awareness, and then you kind of go to, you know, a podcast player or YouTube or wherever to watch the full-length thing,” he said. The new feature is designed to eliminate that extra step by allowing audiences to access complete videos without leaving Instagram. According to reports, creators will also be able to connect up to eight short clips to a single long video, giving users different entry points through which to discover full episodes. The feature, previously tested in Brazil, is now being expanded to selected creators in the United States, according to reports by The Hollywood Reporter and other media outlets. Instagram is also expanding its presence on television screens through Instagram for TV, which supports viewing videos on devices including Apple TV, Samsung, Amazon Fire TV and Google TV. The company is further testing a feature called “Series” to organise episodes of recurring shows and exploring additional ways for users to discover livestreams. The expansion comes as YouTube continues to attract audiences for video podcasts, interviews and other long-form entertainment. Lyons said Instagram wanted to strengthen its position as a destination for social entertainment by giving creators more ways to tell stories and helping audiences discover content. “Our goal is really to be the best place for social entertainment,” she said. “To do that well, we need to broaden the way that we enable people to tell stories through video and enable audiences to discover them,” she added. However, Instagram has yet to announce a comprehensive payment system for creators producing long-form videos comparable to YouTube’s advertising revenue-sharing programme. Mosseri has also acknowledged challenges with previous attempts to introduce broader creator payment programmes, according to Business Insider. For now, the 90-minute video feature remains in testing, with Instagram yet to announce when it will become available to all creators. items.title: LGV : Jet Contractors décroche un marché de 437,6 MDH pour la construction de cinq gares
items.description: L’Office national des chemins de fer (ONCF) a attribué à Jet Contractors le marché de construction de cinq nouvelles gares ferroviaires dans le cadre du projet de ligne à grande vitesse (LGV) entre Kénitra et Marrakech. Le montant de l’offre retenue s’élève à 437,58 millions de dirhams hors taxes, selon les résultats de l’appel d’offres ouvert n° 26T053/PLGV. Le projet prévoit la réalisation de la gare de la ligne à grande vitesse de la Ville verte de Benguérir, ainsi que celle du réseau express régional (RER) dans la même ville. Trois autres gares sont également concernées : Sidi Bou Othmane, Sidi Ghanem et le Grand Stade de Marrakech. Ces infrastructures doivent accompagner le développement des services ferroviaires sur l’axe Kénitra-Marrakech. D’après le document annonçant les résultats de la procédure, Jet Contractors a présenté une offre de 437 575 645,85 dirhams hors taxes, la moins élevée parmi celles jugées conformes aux exigences administratives et techniques du cahier des charges. Le montant retenu dépasse néanmoins l’estimation initiale de l’ONCF, fixée à 385,24 millions de dirhams hors taxes. La différence atteint plus de 52,3 millions de dirhams, soit un dépassement d’environ 13,6 % par rapport au coût prévisionnel du marché. Cette attribution vient conforter la position de Jet Contractors dans les grands chantiers d’infrastructures ferroviaires. En mars dernier, l’entreprise avait déjà remporté le marché de construction de la future gare ferroviaire du Grand Stade de Benslimane, pour un montant de 415,5 millions de dirhams hors taxes. Un programme d’investissement de 96 milliards de dirhams La construction des cinq gares s’inscrit dans le programme d’investissement de l’ONCF, doté d’une enveloppe globale de 96 milliards de dirhams. Celui-ci repose sur trois axes : le développement des infrastructures ferroviaires, le renouvellement et le renforcement du parc de trains, ainsi que l’amélioration des services aux voyageurs. Une enveloppe de 53 milliards de dirhams est consacrée aux infrastructures et aux équipements nécessaires à la ligne à grande vitesse entre Kénitra et Marrakech. L’acquisition de 168 nouveaux trains mobilisera, pour sa part, 29 milliards de dirhams. Les 14 milliards de dirhams restants doivent permettre de préserver la qualité des services et d’assurer la pérennité du réseau ferroviaire existant. À travers ce programme, l’ONCF entend augmenter les capacités du réseau national et renforcer les liaisons entre les villes. L’objectif est de répondre à la progression de la demande de transport ferroviaire tout en adaptant les infrastructures aux besoins générés par les grands projets de développement. items.title: Full list: Winners of the GJA Ashanti Media Excellence Awards
items.description: The Ashanti regional chapter of the Ghana Journalists Association, on Saturday, October 24, recognized and celebrated the impactful work of journalists in the region. The Ashanti Media Excellence Awards were aimed at promoting excellence in journalism and qualitative media practice by recognising and competitively rewarding outstanding journalistic work produced in 2025. The journalists were celebrated for their outstanding storytelling and investigative reporting across 10 competitive categories. Here is the full list of the winners and runners-up for the various categories. Au total, cinq lauréats, dont une région et quatre communes, ont été distingués. La région du Nando s’est illustrée lors de cette cérémonie de récompense des collectivités territoriales performantes, organisée dans le cadre du dispositif d’évaluation des collectivités partenaires du Dispositif d’évaluation des collectivités (DEPAC). Ce mécanisme de récompense repose sur un système d’auto-évaluation des performances des collectivités territoriales, développé et consolidé dans le cadre du DEPAC. Il vise à encourager l’amélioration de la gouvernance locale, le partage des bonnes pratiques et le renforcement des capacités des collectivités. Dans la catégorie des communes, le classement place Koudougou en tête, suivie de Kordié, de Diapangou et de Fada N'Gourma. Les lauréats ont reçu respectivement 13,5 millions, 12 millions, 11 millions et 10 millions de FCFA, accompagnés de trophées et d’attestations. Dans la catégorie des régions, la région du Nando a été récompensée comme collectivité territoriale performante. La région a reçu une enveloppe financière de 15 millions de FCFA.
