items.title: AI’s brain & muscle
items.description: ARTIFICIAL intelligence is usually presented as weightless, almost entirely digital. We ask it to write, calculate, translate or create an image, and the response appears instantly. Yet every answer depends on a substantial physical system. This comprises data centres, specialised processors, cooling equipment etc. In reality AI has both ‘brain’ and ‘muscle’. Algorithms, software, researchers, engineers and companies comprise its brain. Its muscle consists of electricity, computing infrastructure, minerals, manufacturing capacity and reliable networks. The first phase of global AI competition focused mainly on the brain. As AI becomes more widely used, the muscle is becoming impossible to ignore. The International Energy Agency expects electricity demand from data centres to more than double by 2030, with AI a major driver. The challenge is not simply producing more power. It is producing reliable electricity supply and expanded transmission networks to accommodate the needs of large data centres. Oil and gas reserves beneath the ground are not the same as electricity delivered to a data centre. Resources become strategic only when they can be converted into dependable infrastructure. The physical foundations of AI also include copper, aluminium, silicon, and rare-earth materials. Advanced semiconductor technologies depend on specialised materials, while mining and refining remain concentrated in a limited number of countries. The digital economy has not escaped geography! An algorithm can cross a border in milliseconds, but a power plant, mine or factory cannot. This creates a new geopolitical equation. Countries with the strongest AI research and software ecosystems may still depend on others for energy, minerals and manufacturing. Resource-rich countries, meanwhile, may possess the muscle of the AI economy without the universities, capital, software and semiconductor capabilities needed to turn it into computing power. The long-term advantage may belong to countries that can connect the two. The digital economy has not escaped geography. Pakistan illustrates this challenge clearly. It is not currently a leading frontier-AI power and faces serious constraints in reliable electricity, advanced computing, research funding etc. Yet it has a large young population, growing software and IT-services sectors, universities, engineering talent, hydropower and renewable-energy potential, and significant mineral resources. The strategic challenge is therefore not simply to acquire more resources or develop more algorithms, but to connect the country’s physical assets with its scientific and technological capabilities. That would require moving beyond traditional models of exporting raw materials and low-value services. An AI-era strategy would use reliable energy, connectivity and mineral resources to support data centres, cloud services, local research, advanced applications and value-added manufacturing. AI could strengthen sectors such as agriculture, textiles, logistics, mining, health, education and public administration. In this model, AI becomes an industrial multiplier rather than merely another software sector. Resource wealth alone, however, guarantees neither technological independence nor prosperity. Natural resources cannot substitute for universities, skilled workers, capital, innovation and capable institutions. The relationship between AI’s brain and muscle is better understood as multiplication rather than addition. A country with excellent algorithms but unreliable power will struggle to scale, while a country with abundant energy but weak research capacity may remain a commodity supplier. The lesson extends beyond Pakistan. Countries such as the United States have ex­­traordinary stren­gths in research, capital, technology companies and advanced computing. China combines rapidly advancing AI with industrial scale and manufacturing capacity. Gulf countries possess energy and capital, while Australia and Canada have substantial mineral and energy advantages. None controls every part of the AI system. Interdependence will remain unavoidable, but countries that connect more stages, from energy and minerals to computing and applications, will have greater strategic influence. For Pakistan and other natural resource-rich countries, the message is immediate. An AI strategy cannot stop at applications, start-ups or policy statements . It must also address reliable electricity, data-centre infrastructure, digital skills, research institutions, mineral value addition and industrial capacity. The next phase of the AI race will not be decided solely by who builds the smartest models. It will also be decided by who can power them, supply them and apply them productively. AI has a brain. But without muscle, even the most brilliant brain cannot move. The writer is an educationist. Published in Dawn, October 28th, 2026

items.title: Stonebwoy featured on soundtrack for Hollywood action comedy ‘Wrong Toes’
items.description: Ghanaian musician Stonebwoy has joined an international collaboration featured on the official soundtrack of upcoming action comedy Boyz Trip , scheduled for worldwide theatrical release in 2027. The award-winning recording artist features on Wrong Toes , a song bringing together Stonebwoy from Ghana, American recording artist Mashanda Faust and Atlanta-based musical group Hero The Band, blending African and American musical influences. The Boyz Trip entertainment project, comprising the feature film, its original soundtrack and the Wrong Toes music video, is executive produced by Alan Key and Kyle Scott, co-founders of KeyScott Entertainment, headquartered in Brisbane, Australia. The concept for Wrong Toes originated with Alan Key, whose creative vision laid the foundation for the song and its accompanying music video. Kyle Scott spearheaded the creative development and execution of that vision, bringing the project together musically and visually while working alongside recording artist Mashanda Faust to shape the song’s musical direction and overall presentation. Written by Alan Key and Faten El Sayed, Wrong Toes has evolved into an international collaboration featuring artists from Ghana and the United States. The official music video was recently filmed at Cape Town Film Studios in Cape Town, South Africa, with two-time award-winning creative director Warren Gray leading its creative direction. Stonebwoy brings Ghanaian music to the global stage Stonebwoy’s participation presents another opportunity to showcase Ghanaian music through international cinema. Known for his blend of Afrobeats, reggae and dancehall, Stonebwoy contributes his signature sound to a soundtrack designed to connect audiences across Africa, North America, Europe and Australia. His collaboration with American artists Mashanda Faust and Hero The Band also underscores the growing creative relationship between the African and American entertainment industries. Wrong Toes is part of a collection of original music being developed for the Boyz Trip soundtrack through KeyScott Entertainment’s newly launched music division, which focuses on original film music, publishing, artist development and international collaborations. About the film: Boyz Trip Boyz Trip is an upcoming international action comedy starring Desi Banks, Rome Flynn, Algee Smith and South African actor Siv Ngesi. Set against the backdrop of Cape Town, South Africa, the film follows four longtime college friends who reunite for what is supposed to be an unforgettable international vacation. However, their dream getaway quickly spirals into chaos when they become entangled in the dangerous world of a notorious criminal figure known as Le Serpent. What begins as a celebration of friendship turns into an action-packed comedy filled with unexpected twists, dangerous encounters and unforgettable moments. The film blends Hollywood-style action comedy with African culture, international locations and a globally influenced soundtrack. An international production with African roots Boyz Trip is executive produced by Alan Key and Kyle Scott under the banner of KeyScott Entertainment, an international film and television production company headquartered in Brisbane, Australia. The film is directed by Kyle Scott, an American filmmaker and executive producer whose international production experience spans more than 41 countries across six continents. The production team includes: Executive producers: Alan Key and Kyle Scott Director: Kyle Scott Lead producer: Autumn Bailey-Ford Co-producers: Sarsha Venord and Jamez T. Associate producers: Ama K. Abebrese, Lya Castillo and Shayla Hill Global theatrical release and international premieres Boyz Trip is being prepared for an international theatrical rollout in 2027, with official release date announcements expected in early 2027. The production is planning premiere events in five international markets: Cape Town, South Africa Atlanta, Georgia, USA London, England Los Angeles, California, USA Brisbane, Australia Further announcements regarding the film’s theatrical distribution, official soundtrack, music releases and promotional activities are expected as the production approaches its 2027 launch. About KeyScott Entertainment KeyScott Entertainment is an international film, television and music production company based in Brisbane, Australia, focused on developing commercially driven entertainment for global audiences. Through its expanding music division, the company is developing original soundtracks, music publishing opportunities, artist collaborations and new platforms for bringing international musical talent into film and television. The upcoming release of Boyz Trip and its associated soundtrack forms part of the company’s broader vision to connect storytelling, music and culture across international markets.

items.title: Nigeria would be rich if leaders left public funds in banks – Obi
items.description: Former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi has said Nigeria would be significantly wealthier if leaders left public funds in banks to generate interest instead of mismanaging the country’s resources. Obi, who is the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) for the 2027 general elections, made the statement during an interview with a radio station in Nasarawa State on Wednesday, where he spoke about his administration’s approach to public spending, accountability and his record in basic education. The former Labour Party presidential candidate argued that the country could have accumulated substantial wealth if public office holders consistently protected government funds and allowed them to earn interest in financial institutions. “I wish everybody in this country left money in the bank; they have interest. Nigeria would have been so rich that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi disclosed that the funds under his administration were kept in three different banks, presenting the decision as an example of prudent management of public resources. He also lamented what he described as a culture of dishonesty and the tendency to discredit people who act with integrity in Nigeria. “Nigeria is a criminalised place. The criminals will always come together to show what the honest person did,” he said. The former governor further criticised what he described as a reversal of moral values, arguing that people who act honestly are often treated as though they have committed wrongdoing. “In Nigeria, to be honest is to be a criminal. To be criminal is to be honest,” Obi said. He added that Nigeria would have accumulated far greater wealth if its leaders had consistently left public funds in banks rather than diverting them. “We would have been worth so much that we don’t know what to do with money,” he said. Obi also addressed questions surrounding his administration’s public engagements, explaining that he believed the results of government projects should speak for themselves because they were financed with public funds. “We did what we were doing with public money, so the public already see us working, so why are we going to do the ceremony or showing it on TV? Maybe I was wrong, but that was what happened,” he said. The former governor also defended his record in basic education, insisting that Anambra performed exceptionally well in the sector during his tenure. “I was the best in education, basic education as a governor. You can go and check the records,” he said. He cited a visit by Professor Paul Collier of the University of Oxford, whom he said visited several states to assess developments in education and witnessed significant improvements. Obi maintained that education was a key measure of development and argued that his administration’s performance in the sector demonstrated the impact of responsible leadership. items.title: Brésil : battu par Lula da Silva, Flávio Bolsonaro trouve refuge aux États-Unis
items.description: Washington vole au secours de Flávio Bolsonaro. Deux jours apres sa defaite a l'election presidentielle bresilienne face a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, le fils de l'ancien president Jair Bolsonaro a obtenu l'assurance de pouvoir entrer aux etats-Unis avec sa famille. Mardi 27 octobre, un haut responsable du departement d'etat americain a confirme que des visas leur seraient delivres, alors que le candidat conservateur fait l'objet de plusieurs enquetes judiciaires au Bresil. Âge de 45 ans, Flávio Bolsonaro a ete battu au second tour par le president sortant. Refusant initialement de reconnaître sa defaite, le senateur avait denonce des irregularites electorales, sans pour autant apporter d'elements permettant d'etayer ses accusations. Lula a remporte plus de 64 millions de voix, contre moins de 60 millions pour son adversaire. Une famille engluee dans des histoires de corruption La decision americaine intervient dans un contexte judiciaire particulierement sensible. Flávio Bolsonaro est notamment vise par des investigations portant sur des soupcons de corruption, de blanchiment d'argent et de fraude fiscale, accusations qu'il conteste. Lundi 26 octobre, le juge Alexandre de Moraes, membre de la Cour supreme bresilienne, avait ordonne la remise de ses passeports et lui avait interdit de quitter le territoire. Malgre cette decision, plusieurs medias bresiliens et americains rapportent que le senateur aurait rejoint la Floride , ou reside notamment son frere Eduardo. Ce depart souleve desormais des interrogations sur les relations entre Brasília et Washington. Donald Trump, proche de la famille Bolsonaro, avait soutenu le candidat conservateur et critique le deroulement de l'election, sans presenter de preuves de fraude. Pour l'administration americaine, l'octroi de visas constitue un nouveau geste politique en faveur du clan Bolsonaro, deja fragilise par l'incarceration de l'ancien president Jair Bolsonaro. Reste a determiner si Flávio Bolsonaro entend s'installer durablement aux etats-Unis ou organiser depuis l'etranger une riposte politique et judiciaire. Son depart pourrait aussi compliquer la recomposition de la droite bresilienne apres sa defaite electorale.

items.title: Le SNJT exige le droit du journaliste Zied El Heni à un procès équitable
items.description: La chambre criminelle spécialisée dans les affaires de terrorisme a condamné, mardi soir, 27 octobre 2026, le journaliste Zied El Heni à une peine de quatre ans de prison, dans une affaire liée à son travail journalistique concernant ce qui est connu sous le nom d’«enregistrements sonores», a rapporté le Syndicat national des journalistes tunisiens (SNJT) dans un communiqué publié sur sa page Facebook officielle , en réclamant la révision de cette décision et en exigeant que le droit à un procès équitable soit garanti au journaliste et que toutes les garanties de la défense soient respectées. Le syndicat a précisé que les poursuites judiciaires contre El Heni ont fait suite à son audition en tant que témoin dans l’affaire des enregistrements sonores impliquant l’homme politique Mondher Ounissi , ancien secrétaire général du parti Ennahdha. Il a été interrogé sur ses relations avec ses sources d’information dans ce dossier, avant que son statut juridique ne soit requalifié en celui d’accusé. Tunisie | Des activistes politiques condamnés à des peines de 4 à 25 ans de prison Selon le même communiqué, le journaliste Zied El Heni fait face à quatre chefs d’accusation en vertu de la loi relative à la lutte contre le terrorisme et le blanchiment d’argent : constitution d’une organisation terroriste, divulgation de secrets au profit de ladite organisation, non-dénonciation d’un crime terroriste, et prise de contact avec des agents d’un État étranger en vue de les inciter à porter atteinte aux intérêts du pays. Le syndicat a, par ailleurs, appelé à mettre fin aux poursuites judiciaires — qualifiées d’arbitraires — engagées contre des journalistes en raison de leur travail professionnel ou de leurs opinions, tout en insistant sur la nécessité de respecter la confidentialité des sources journalistiques et de les protéger contre toute forme d’atteinte ou de pression. Le SNJT a également appelé à mettre un terme à l’instrumentalisation des lois et des procédures judiciaires visant pour restreindre la liberté d’expression et le travail journalistique. Le Syndicat a, par ailleurs, exhorté les autorités politiques à assumer leurs responsabilités et à prendre des mesures concrètes pour faire cesser les restrictions, garantir l’indépendance de la presse et assurer le respect de la liberté d’expression. En conclusion de son communiqué, le SNJT a affirmé que la protection des journalistes et de la confidentialité de leurs sources constitue un engagement non négociable, soulignant que s’en prendre à un seul journaliste représente une menace pour la liberté de la presse ainsi que pour le droit de la société à disposer d’une information libre et indépendante. I. B. L’article Le SNJT exige le droit du journaliste Zied El Heni à un procès équitable est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Collision entre deux trains en Espagne : le bilan grimpe à 46 morts
items.description: Le bilan de la collision entre deux trains survenue en Espagne s’est alourdi à au moins 46 morts, selon les médias espagnols citant les services de la Protection civile. L’accident, survenu le 28 octobre dans la région de Castille-La Manche, a également fait 179 blessés. Les secours restent mobilisés tandis que les circonstances du drame font l’objet d’une enquête. Le bilan humain de la collision entre deux trains en Espagne continue de s’alourdir. Selon les informations rapportées par les médias espagnols, au moins 46 personnes ont perdu la vie et 179 autres ont été blessées dans cet accident ferroviaire survenu à proximité d’Urda, en Castille-La Manche, à environ 150 kilomètres au sud de Madrid. L’accident a impliqué un train de la compagnie Iryo et un train de la compagnie publique Renfe. À la suite du drame, la circulation ferroviaire sur la ligne reliant Madrid à l’Andalousie a été interrompue. Les équipes de secours ont été déployées sur place pour porter assistance aux victimes et poursuivre les opérations. Les autorités s’attachent également à établir les circonstances exactes de la collision. Une enquête a été ouverte afin de déterminer les causes de l’accident. Selon des informations rapportées par le quotidien El País, une erreur humaine pourrait être envisagée, notamment en lien avec un problème touchant le système de sécurité et une instruction de circulation. Le président du gouvernement espagnol, Pedro Sánchez, a exprimé sa profonde émotion après l’accident. Dans un message publié sur le réseau social X, il s’est dit « consterné » par le drame et a exprimé sa solidarité avec les victimes, leurs proches et les personnes touchées. The post Collision entre deux trains en Espagne : le bilan grimpe à 46 morts appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: France 2030 : la Cour des comptes alerte sur un «mur budgétaire»
items.description: Dans un rapport publie le 27 octobre, les magistrats de la Cour des comptes dressent un bilan a mi-parcours nuance du programme lance en octobre 2021 pour relancer l'industrie et l'innovation . Ils saluent un deploiement rapide, mais soulignent de reelles fragilites budgetaires et organisationnelles. Fin 2025, plus de 7 300 projets avaient fait l'objet d'un contrat pour un total de 33,4 milliards d'euros. Seuls 14 milliards ont deja ete decaisses, laissant plus de 19 milliards a verser. La Cour evoque ainsi « un mur d'engagements budgetaires a financer dans les prochaines annees » et un « enjeu de soutenabilite », dans un contexte de finances publiques tendues. Le plan repose a 82 % sur des subventions, l'outil le plus coûteux pour l'etat. Les magistrats deplorent des « effets d'aubaine » : selon une enquete du Secretariat general pour l'investissement, pres de la moitie des projets finances auraient vu le jour meme sans le soutien public. L'economiste Philippe Herlin fustige un « scandale dont on ne parle pas assez », estimant qu'il faut recuperer les 19 milliards d'euros qui doivent encore etre verses. 🔴#France2030, un scandale dont on ne parle pas assez Un plan de 54 MILLIARDS D'EUROS versés de façon discrétionnaire. Des chiffres bidons : "5,4 euros de richesse supplémentaire à long terme pour un euro investi". Si c'était vrai, vu son niveau de dépenses publiques, la France serait le pays le plus riche du monde ! La Cour des comptes dénonce une "absence réelle de priorisations au risque de disperser les moyens de l'État" 19 milliards d'euros doivent encore être versés. IL FAUT LES RÉCUPÉRER ! — Philippe Herlin (@philippeherlin) October 28, 2026 France 2030 a surtout permis, selon la Cour, d'accelerer ou d'amplifier des initiatives deja prevues. Les grandes entreprises, mieux armees pour mettre les etats en concurrence, sont paradoxalement les plus demandeuses d'aides. Lance « sans reflexion suffisante » et sans coordination reelle avec les programmes europeens, le dispositif souffre aussi d'un manque de priorisation. Deja en 2021, le plan France 2030 avait ete tres largement critique par les oppositions qui y voyaient de la « propagande » d'un « pompier pyromane » . Les efforts se dispersent entre de nombreux objectifs sectoriels, et l'etat peine a interrompre les projets moins convaincants. Sur X, l'analyste Olivier Durnez a souligne : « 33,4 Md€ engages, 14 Md€ verses. La facture reste devant nous. » France 2030 : 33,4 Md€ engagés, 14 Md€ versés. La facture reste devant nous. La Cour des comptes publie ce soir son bilan à mi-parcours du plan à 54 Md€ lancé en 2021. 🔴 82 % des aides aux entreprises sont des subventions, la forme la plus coûteuse. 🔴 1 % des projets concentrent 49 % des montants. 🔴 Moins de 10 % des projets terminés fin 2025. ✅ Déploiement rapide : les crédits ont été engagés massivement. Engager vite, c'est facile. Le pilotage commence quand il faut décaisser et mesurer ce que ça rapporte. Vous signeriez 19 Md€ de reste à payer sans calendrier de décaissement ? — Olivier Durnez (@OlivierDurnez) October 27, 2026 La Cour refuse de se prononcer sur un eventuel successeur au plan, mais recommande de privilegier les leviers non financiers (reglementation, achat public) et de reserver les subventions en dernier recours. Matignon promet un pilotage plus fin et un recentrage sur quelques domaines strategiques comme l'intelligence artificielle ou le quantique.

items.description: La commission chargée d'enquêter sur la mort en détention, en septembre dernier, de 37 personnes soupçonnées d'orpaillage dans l'État du Niger, au Nigeria, a rendu son rapport mardi 27 octobre. Elle pointe sévèrement des officiers des « Mining Marshals », une unité paramilitaire du Corps de sécurité et de défense civile du Nigeria. Elle recommande le versement d'indemnités aux survivants et aux familles des victimes, dont 14 enfants.

items.title: 15 boulettes de cocaïne présumée saisies chez un étudiant
items.description: Un homme se présentant comme étudiant a été déféré au parquet à Dakar, au Sénégal pour trafic présumé de cocaïne et tentative de corruption, selon un communiqué de la police sénégalaise, le mardi 27 octobre 2026. Quinze boulettes de drogue, d’un poids total annoncé de 205 grammes, auraient été découvertes dans sa chambre lors d’une opération policière déclenchée par un renseignement anonyme. L’enquête a été ouverte à la suite d’un signalement faisant état d’un réseau présumé de trafic de drogue entre la Médina et Yoff, notamment, dans le secteur de Diamalaye. Selon les informations communiquées par la police, le mardi 27 octobre 2026, les investigations menées par le commissariat d’arrondissement de la Médina ont permis d’identifier un suspect, puis de le placer sous surveillance. Les policiers se sont ensuite rendus à son domicile pour une perquisition. Dans une valise dissimulée sous des vêtements, ils ont découvert quinze boulettes présentées comme de la cocaïne, pour un poids total annoncé de 205 grammes. Le suspect aurait également tenté de corrompre les agents lors de son transfert au commissariat, en leur proposant de l’argent en échange de sa libération. À l’issue de la procédure, il a été déféré au parquet pour les faits présumés de trafic de cocaïne et de tentative de corruption. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article 15 boulettes de cocaïne présumée saisies chez un étudiant est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Non, Modou Ngom n’est pas condamné à mort aux États-Unis (Fact-cheking)
items.description: Une publication diffusée sur Facebook le 2 octobre 2026 affirme que Modou Ngom, présenté comme Sénégalais, a été condamné à mort aux États-Unis après un accident de la route ayant coûté la vie à trois personnes dans l'Ohio. La justice de l'Ohio a-t-elle prononcé une condamnation à mort contre lui ? Capture d'écran de la publication Facebook de Rama Sonko, 2 octobre 2026. L'accident du 11 avril 2026 sur l'I-71 Dans un communiqué publié le 12 avril 2026 , la police routière de l'Ohio (Ohio State Highway Patrol) indique qu'un accident impliquant neuf véhicules s'est produit la veille, vers 18 h 27, sur les voies nord de l'Interstate 71, près de l'échangeur avec la U.S. 36, dans le comté de Delaware. Selon ce communiqué, le semi-remorque conduit par Modou Ngom, 50 ans, domicilié à Columbus, ne s'est pas arrêté à l'approche d'un ralentissement dans une zone de travaux. Il a percuté par l'arrière plusieurs véhicules à l'arrêt. Un homme de 37 ans, une femme de 36 ans et un enfant d'un an, tous trois domiciliés à Ashley et circulant dans le même véhicule, ont été tués. La presse locale les a identifiés comme Luke Soposki, son épouse Lynnea et leur fils Logan. Selon la police routière, trois autres personnes ont été soignées pour des blessures ne mettant pas leur vie en danger. Le 13 avril, dans sa réquisition sur la caution déposée devant le tribunal du comté de Delaware, le procureur adjoint Mark Sleeper a affirmé qu'une caméra du département des Transports de l'Ohio montrait que le conducteur n'avait tenté ni de freiner ni d'éviter les véhicules. L'identité du conducteur Le 23 avril 2026, le directeur du département de la Sécurité publique de l'Ohio, Andy Wilson, a publié une déclaration selon laquelle Modou Ngom serait entré aux États-Unis dans les années 1990 et aurait utilisé plusieurs noms et dates de naissance pour obtenir des pièces d'identité. D'après ce texte, les registres de l'État montrent qu'il a repris le nom de Modou Ngom en 2015. Selon le même responsable , il a été naturalisé citoyen américain sous une autre identité. L' acte d'accusation le désigne comme Modou F. Ngom, également connu sous le nom de Lamine Gaye. La défense a demandé l'abandon des poursuites en soutenant que ces déclarations publiques portaient atteinte au droit de l'accusé à un procès équitable. Aucun des documents publics consultés n'établit sa nationalité d'origine. L'inculpation et le procès Le droit de l'Ohio classe les crimes, appelés felonies, en cinq degrés, du premier, le plus grave, au cinquième. Le 16 avril 2026, un grand jury du comté de Delaware a inculpé Modou Ngom de trois chefs d'homicide aggravé au volant, crimes du troisième degré, et de quatre chefs de blessures au volant, crimes du quatrième degré. Le dossier a été confié à la juge Marianne Hemmeter, du tribunal des plaids communs du comté. Le verdict porte sur cinq chefs de blessures. Les documents publics consultés ne précisent pas à quel moment ce cinquième chef a été ajouté. Le procès s'est ouvert le mardi 22 septembre 2026 devant un jury de douze personnes, nombre imposé pour toute affaire de crime par la règle 23 de procédure pénale de l'Ohio . Le 25 septembre, Modou Ngom a témoigné . Il a déclaré qu'il empruntait régulièrement ce tronçon pour son travail et qu'il voyait ce jour-là pour la première fois la bretelle réduite à une seule voie. Il a expliqué qu'il regardait son rétroviseur latéral pour se déporter sur la voie de gauche lorsqu'il n'a pas vu les véhicules arrêtés devant lui. L'accusation a soutenu que la vidéo de l'accident contredisait cette version. Après près de deux heures de délibération, le jury l'a déclaré coupable des huit chefs. En Ohio, un tel verdict doit être unanime , écrit et signé par tous les jurés. La fixation de la peine En Ohio, la déclaration de culpabilité ne fixe pas la peine. L'article 2929.19 du Code révisé impose au tribunal de tenir une audience distincte avant de condamner une personne reconnue coupable d'un crime. L'accusé, le procureur et les victimes ou leurs représentants peuvent y présenter des éléments. Avant de se prononcer, le juge examine le dossier, le rapport d'enquête sur la personnalité de l'accusé lorsqu'il en existe un, et les déclarations des victimes sur les conséquences des faits. C'est donc la juge, et non le jury, qui fixera la peine de Modou Ngom. L'audience est programmée le 29 octobre 2026 à 8 h 30. Les peines prévues par la loi L'article 2903.06 qualifie d'homicide aggravé au volant le fait de causer la mort d'autrui en conduisant, soit sous l’emprise de l'alcool ou de stupéfiants, soit par imprudence. Commis par imprudence, il constitue un crime du troisième degré. L'article 2903.08 punit de la même manière le fait de blesser gravement autrui par imprudence au volant, qualifié de crime du quatrième degré. L'article 2929.14 fixe la durée de la prison pour chaque chef. Chacun des trois homicides est passible de 12 à 60 mois, soit d'un à cinq ans. Chacun des cinq chefs de blessures est passible de 6 à 18 mois, soit de six mois à un an et demi. Si la juge retenait la durée maximale pour chaque chef, les trois homicides représenteraient 15 ans et les cinq chefs de blessures 7 ans et demi. Le total de 22 ans et demi ne vaut toutefois que si les peines sont exécutées l'une après l'autre. Le même article ne permet ce cumul que si la juge constate qu'il est nécessaire pour protéger le public ou punir l'accusé, qu'il n'est pas disproportionné, et qu'au moins une circonstance supplémentaire est réunie, par exemple un dommage si grave qu'aucune peine unique ne suffit à en refléter la gravité. Les crimes passibles de la peine de mort en Ohio L'article 2929.04 réserve la peine de mort au meurtre aggravé. Il exige en outre qu'au moins une des dix circonstances suivantes figure dans l'acte d'accusation et soit prouvée au-delà de tout doute raisonnable. Ces circonstances sont l'assassinat du président des États-Unis, du gouverneur ou d'un candidat à ces fonctions, un meurtre commis contre rémunération, un meurtre commis pour échapper à des poursuites, un meurtre commis en détention ou après une évasion, un meurtre commis par une personne déjà condamnée pour un meurtre intentionnel ou dans le cadre de plusieurs meurtres intentionnels, le meurtre d'un policier, un meurtre commis au cours d'un enlèvement, d'un viol, d'un incendie criminel aggravé, d'un vol aggravé ou d'un cambriolage aggravé, le meurtre d'un témoin, le meurtre intentionnel d'un enfant de moins de 13 ans, et un meurtre commis au cours d'un acte de terrorisme. Le meurtre aggravé lui-même, défini à l'article 2903.01 , suppose d'avoir causé la mort intentionnellement. Les homicides retenus contre Modou Ngom relèvent de l'imprudence au volant. Il n'a été ni poursuivi ni reconnu coupable de meurtre aggravé. La réponse de l'avocat de la défense Contacté par courriel le 22 octobre 2026, l'avocat de Modou Ngom, Jeffery M. Poth, a indiqué ne pas pouvoir commenter les détails de l'affaire avant l'audience de fixation de la peine prévue le 29 octobre 2026. Il a toutefois confirmé par écrit que son client n'encourt pas la peine de mort, tout en précisant qu'il pourrait être condamné à plus de vingt ans de prison. Cette estimation concorde avec le maximum de 22 ans et demi qui résulte du Code révisé. Capture d'écran de la réponse de Jeffery M. Poth, avocat de Modou Ngom, reçue par courriel le 22 octobre 2026. Conclusion Au 28 octobre 2026, Modou Ngom a été reconnu coupable de huit chefs liés à l'accident du 11 avril 2026, mais aucune peine n'a été prononcée. Les infractions retenues sont punies de prison par le droit de l'Ohio et ne figurent pas parmi celles qui peuvent entraîner la peine de mort, ce que son avocat confirme. La peine sera fixée par la juge lors de l'audience prévue le 29 octobre 2026. Yaya SOW

items.title: Claves para formar Gobierno en Israel tras las elecciones o regresar a las urnas: consulta del presidente, negociación y votación
items.description: Tras las reñidas elecciones legislativas de este martes, las primeras tras los ataques de Hamás del 7 de octubre de 2023 y la brutal ofensiva en Gaza , Israel encara ahora un arduo proceso que podría durar hasta alrededor de tres meses para dotarse de un nuevo Ejecutivo o volver a las urnas si ninguno de los dos grandes bloques en liza logra reunir suficientes apoyos. Ni el bando que respalda al primer ministro Benjamín Netanyahu ni el de sus rivales —encabezados por el general retirado Gadi Eisenkot — dispone de una mayoría que les permita formar un Ejecutivo sin otros apoyos. El resultado de las negociaciones que se abrirán la semana próxima está en el aire y todo apunta a que dependerá, no solo del respaldo de las dos listas de partidos árabes, que casi han duplicado su representación parlamentaria, sino también de la voluntad real del bloque opositor de pactar con ellos. items.title: Célébration de la 14ᵉ édition de l’Éthique & Compliance Days sous le thème « L’intégrité au quotidien : nos choix font la différence ».
items.description: Conakry, le 27 octobre 2026 – Célébration de la 14ᵉ édition de l’Éthique & Compliance Days sous le thème « L’intégrité au quotidien : nos choix font la différence » Orange Guinée célèbre la 14ᵉ édition des Éthique & Compliance Days, son rendez-vous annuel consacré à la promotion de l’éthique, de la conformité et de la responsabilité au sein de l’Entreprise et auprès de ses parties prenantes. Placée sous le thème « L’intégrité au quotidien : nos choix font la différence », cette édition rappelle que l’intégrité ne se manifeste pas seulement dans les grandes décisions. Elle se traduit aussi dans les choix et les comportements de chaque jour, à tous les niveaux de l’organisation. À l’ouverture de cette semaine de sensibilisation, le Directeur général d’Orange Guinée, M. Ousmane Boly TRAORE, a souligné le rôle essentiel de l’intégrité dans la confiance accordée à l’Entreprise par ses clients, ses partenaires, ses collaborateurs et l’ensemble de ses parties prenantes. Chaque décision prise dans le cadre professionnel contribue à renforcer cette confiance et à la préserver. Dans un contexte où les attentes en matière de gouvernance, de transparence et de responsabilité sont croissantes, Orange Guinée est convaincue que l’éthique et la conformité contribuent à une performance durable et à la création de valeur à long terme. Plusieurs initiatives rythment cette 14ᵉ édition afin de renforcer la culture de l’intégrité et d’encourager l’adoption de comportements responsables. Un webinaire a réuni les collaborateurs autour des enjeux de l’intégrité dans les activités professionnelles. Les échanges ont notamment porté sur le rôle des décisions individuelles dans la prévention des risques, la préservation de la réputation de l’Entreprise et la promotion d’un environnement de travail fondé sur la confiance et le respect. Orange Guinée porte également une attention particulière à ses partenaires d’affaires, afin de promouvoir des relations fondées sur des principes partagés d’intégrité, de transparence et de responsabilité. Cette semaine a été aussi l’occasion de rappeler aux collaborateurs et aux tiers les dispositifs mis à leur disposition pour prévenir et signaler les situations contraires aux principes éthiques du Groupe : Hello Ethics (la plateforme de signalement des alertes éthiques, https://orange.integrityline.org ) et Lannayah (l’outil interne de déclaration des conflits d’intérêts). À travers cette 14ᵉ édition de l’Éthics & Compliance Days, Orange Guinée réaffirme son engagement à faire de l’intégrité un réflexe quotidien et un principe directeur dans l’ensemble de ses activités.

items.title: Titre de séjour : ignorée par la préfecture des Hauts-de-Seine, une Algérienne saisit la justice
items.description: Les revers judiciaires se multiplient pour une administration française parfois expéditive dans le refus des demandes de titres de séjour ou de renouvellement introduites par les ressortissants algériens. Une Algérienne installée légalement depuis 2023 en France vient de faire plier la préfecture des Hauts-de-Seine qui a ignoré la demande de renouvellement de son certificat de résidence. Demande déposée en décembre 2024, la préfecture ne répond pas Selon les explications de son avocat, Me Fayçal Megherbi , la plaignante a introduit une demande de renouvellement de son titre de séjour “vie privée et familiale” auprès de la préfecture des Hauts-de-Seine en décembre 2024, mais l’administration s'est confinée dans un silence synonyme de rejet implicite de la demande. Les services préfectoraux “n’ont même pas daigné produire d'observations en défense pour justifier leur position”, indique Me Megherbi, avocat spécialiste du droit des étrangers. La solution dans ce genre de situation, c'est le recours à la justice administrative qui, décidément, constitue un véritable contrepoids aux abus de l'administration. La justice administrative tranche en faveur de la ressortissante algérienne Le tribunal administratif de Cergy-Pontoise est saisi par la voie du référé. Première bonne nouvelle pour la requérante, le juge a considéré que “la condition d'urgence, traditionnellement présumée en matière de refus ou de renouvellement de titre de séjour, était bel et bien remplie”. Dans sa décision rendue mardi 27 octobre, le tribunal a souligné “une méconnaissance manifeste des stipulations de l'article 6-2 de l'accord franco-algérien du 27 décembre 1968, créant ainsi un doute sérieux quant à la légalité de la décision attaquée”. Jugeant la décision de l’administration “illégale”, le tribunal a prononcé la suspension du refus implicite opposé au renouvellement du titre de séjour de la ressortissante algérienne et intimé au préfet des Hauts-de-Seine de procéder à “un réexamen complet de la situation de la requérante dans un délai resserré de deux mois.” En attendant, l'administration est contrainte de lui délivrer une autorisation provisoire de séjour valant autorisation de travail. Aussi, l'État est condamné à lui verser la somme de 1000 euros au titre des frais de justice. Cette décision rappelle que “le respect des procédures et des accords internationaux s'impose aux représentants de l'État dans les départements”, commente Me Megherbi. L’article Titre de séjour : ignorée par la préfecture des Hauts-de-Seine, une Algérienne saisit la justice est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: The Best Kind of Book Adaptation
items.description: The couple seated next to me at the Metropolitan Opera’s latest world premiere did not stay for the second act; perhaps they didn’t appreciate the puppeteered genitalia that unfurled onstage shortly after the curtain rose. I understood their alarm. After watching a dress rehearsal a week earlier, I had texted my boyfriend: “I am shocked by the size of Hans Vollman’s puppet penis.” Vollman is one of the central characters in Lincoln in the Bardo , adapted by the composer Missy Mazzoli and the librettist Royce Vavrek from George Saunders’s Booker Prize–winning 2017 novel of the same name . Like almost everyone else in the tale, Vollman is dead but in profound denial about that fact—in his case, because he can’t reckon with the tragedy of having expired before he could consummate his new marriage. Hence the outsize appendage: a perpetual reminder of Vollman’s unfinished business. It may seem puerile for one of the most prominent opera companies in the world to put such effort into illustrating the undignified source of Vollman’s grief. In fact, although the puppet might make audiences laugh—or leave—it’s a striking symbol of why operatic adaptations of literature can be so exciting. At a moment when film or TV versions of novels often end up, at best, as decent airplane watches, opera, as the excellent Lincoln in the Bardo illustrates, has the potential to create something bolder and more bizarre. Opera’s lingering reputation for being stuffy and elitist has helped obscure a fundamental truth about the medium: It’s weird. Even before modern composers started testing the limits of storytelling, operas tended to be guided by minimal logic; if you’d like to feel exceptionally confused, I suggest reading a synopsis of Richard Wagner ’s Tannhäuser . And the form relies on artifice to function. There is nothing naturalistic about characters conversing in song with the kind of vocal power and dexterity that could make a skeptic believe in God. This means that there is effectively no such thing as a shy opera—at least not one that stands the test of time. Any opera that succeeds must quickly teach audiences to understand that what they’re going to experience won’t obey the laws of many other forms of entertainment—the kinds in which plot developments are reasonably justified, characters don’t share their every thought in repetitive and excruciating detail, and the gates of hell don’t suddenly open in a dining-room floor. [ Read: George Saunders has a new mantra ] This makes opera a natural fit for Lincoln in the Bardo , a not-very-realistic novel that’s written almost entirely in dialogue. Saunders’s book is set the night after the burial of President Abraham Lincoln’s 11-year-old son, Willie, and is narrated by more than 150 voices, most of them belonging to Willie’s new neighbors in Oak Hill Cemetery in Washington, D.C. Some become Willie’s spiritual guides: the Reverend Everly Thomas, the frustrated Vollman, and a young gay man named Roger Bevins III. Others are stranger and more profane. Some souls have suffered greatly, most notably the enslaved people buried outside the cemetery boundaries, and some have inflicted suffering, including an enslaver whose streams of pure bigotry are difficult to read. As Thomas, Vollman, and Bevins urge Willie to leave the bardo—a space between life and the afterlife, as defined in Buddhism, that’s dangerous for children—the living Lincoln wanders among them. His grief, more than anything else, is what keeps Willie from moving on to whatever comes next. I’ve been trying to imagine what a Hollywood adaptation of this astonishing tonal chaos could possibly look like. (One is in the works , a hybrid live-action, stop-motion film in which Tom Hanks will play the president.) In recent years, the often risk-averse studio system has favored, with notable exceptions such as the joyously bizarro Poor Things , literary adaptations that hew to basic genre constraints: status-cast thrillers with blockbuster aspirations such as The Housemaid and Verity ; prestige limited series, à la East of Eden , that seem destined to wither away algorithmically as they roll off the Netflix queue; and, as ever, the endless iterations of 19th-century British novels, including the recent Sense and Sensibility and the dubious, upcoming Ebenezer . There remains room, in that milieu, for real artistry, but perhaps not for a choice as wild and possibly alienating as the Met’s X-rated puppet. Without the freedom to be truly outlandish, could an adaptation really do justice to Bardo ? I can’t envision a version of the novel that waters down its most outré choices but also manages to preserve its magic. An opera adaptation of Bardo must, of course, pare back. Many dozens of well-defined characters bounding across the stage would be exciting, but also impractical. Yet it needn’t water down: A successful opera is big, and also strange. That’s especially true now; opera companies including the Met , recognizing the need to attract younger audiences, have put more emphasis on developing new works that can make the old form seem fresh. That shift has seemed to breed greater comfort with challenging choices. Among the many contemporary operas the Met has premiered in recent years are a new version of the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice narrated by three stones—yes, stones—and a harsh, mind-bending adaptation of Luis Buñuel’s surrealist film The Exterminating Angel . Lincoln in the Bardo —the opera—is hugely entertaining. It’s full of apt little musical jokes; the most spiritually harrowing scene, in which Reverend Thomas recounts his journey to the bardo, is repeatedly interrupted by the ludicrous ditties of a “doodling Pennsylvanian.” But the show also embraces, and enhances, many of the most difficult elements of Saunders’s novel. The creators have made the striking decision, for instance, to have a teenage girl named Elise Traynor, who is trapped in the bardo in a state of grisly eternal torment, be portrayed by a male countertenor. The uncanniness of watching an adult man take the guise of a young girl helps make that girl’s plight more visceral. It is a constant reminder, almost below the level of awareness, that Elise will never reach maturity. She won’t have the chance to discover what kind of adult she might be—deep-voiced or dulcet-toned, rebellious or traditional, effeminate or masculine. [ Read: The art of book-to-film adaptations ] That kind of layered creativity represents opera’s literary capabilities at their best. A great book creates a private emotional landscape inside the reader: a kind of internal set piece that contains the characters, the space they occupy, and the feelings they provoke. When I open the book Lincoln in the Bardo , I also travel to the tiny, three-dimensional model of it that lives somewhere between my mind and my heart. Opera, like film, can’t re-create the personal experience of reading; the characters will never look just as you pictured them. But it can create an accentuating mirror to that experience. In my imagined version of Saunders’s bardo, Elise Traynor now has a voice. Because that voice isn’t quite what I expected, I’ve started to think about the character in new, unsettling, enriching ways. Because of the opera, she’s taken on a bit more of a life of her own. The most haunting refrain in Lincoln in the Bardo belongs to young Willie Lincoln. Unsure of where he is and why, and desperate to be reunited with his parents, he invents a credo for how he will get home: “never if weak, maybe if strong.” The audience knows his case is hopeless, but it’s impossible not to be moved by his innocent courage, or by the sweet, mournful instrumentation that accompanies it. His words also function as something like an ethos for the opera itself: To stand a chance at success, it must do the thing with bravery, no holds barred.

items.title: How American Girl Doll Lost Its Way
items.description: Photographs by Elizabeth Renstrom for The Atlantic In the early 1990s, when I was in elementary school, a fancy catalog would arrive in the mailbox of our 1950s split-level in Philadelphia four times a year, and I’d hurry to my room to pore over its elaborate spreads. Tea caddies, Windsor chairs, writing quills, ice-cream churns. We didn’t have any antiques in our home, but the lure of the past was so strong that sometimes my sisters, five and seven years older than me, crammed onto my bed to dog-ear the pages too. Most of all, we looked forward to checking in with the girls arrayed there, whose stories we knew so well: Samantha, Molly, Kirsten, Felicity, Addy, and, later in the decade, Josefina. They were the American Girl dolls, preadolescents just slightly older than me, and I was enthralled by the pictures of their period dresses, tiny school supplies, and exotic waxed lunch foods. My own doll was the farm girl Kirsten Larson, a Swedish immigrant to 1850s Minnesota. She had come in a burgundy box, with a slim book titled Meet Kirsten tucked in beside her. I promptly begged for the five other Kirsten books; the historical-fiction series followed the same pattern for each doll, ushering her through a year’s worth of life events, tailored to her personality and time and place. I remember playing with Kirsten in the backyard and having her trace out symbols in the dirt, just as she did with her new friend, a Dakota girl called Singing Bird, in the second book, Kirsten Learns a Lesson . To have such a doll was to own a whole world and the narratives within it. In my blue-collar neighborhood, we lucky doll owners felt that our Boomer parents had entrusted us with a valuable possession, and they had. When they were first introduced, in 1986, American Girl dolls cost a shocking $68 (roughly $208 today). Almost every Millennial I know who once spent hours with her American Girl doll has kept it, lovingly, into adulthood. The dolls’ hardscrabble backstories piqued curiosity about the past. Kirsten’s best friend died of cholera on the journey from Sweden; Samantha Parkington, the wealthy “Victorian beauty” living in 1904 Westchester County, New York, was an orphan; Molly McIntire’s doctor father was off serving in World War II England. Each doll confronted challenges in her young life that felt at once intimate and unfamiliar. Add well-made accessories and vivid history to the mix, and girlhood acquired an allure that Barbie seemed to bypass on her way to her plastic Dreamhouse. Yet as American Girl’s 40th anniversary arrives, the brand finds itself in something of a midlife crisis. In 1998, Pleasant Rowland, the former teacher and textbook writer who’d dreamed up the dolls, sold Pleasant Company to an unlikely steward: Mattel, the company behind Barbie and her stilettos. A quarter century later, the heyday of preteen devotion to playmates from bygone eras seems like, well, a bygone era. Mattel’s dire balance sheets for the American Girl line confirm that the magic has faded. Might a surge of celebratory attention to the Pleasant Company past be the secret to renewed relevance? It certainly could not be better timed, with the Millennial faithful now in their childbearing—and toy-buying—years. With Rowland’s spare-no-effort ethos of product creation clearly in mind, Mattel has released The Making of American Girl , a chronicle of Pleasant Company’s origin story that resembles the sumptuous catalogs of my childhood, only far grander in scale. The coffee-table book is a canny paean to the dozen years of Rowland’s leadership. Extolling her “courage and conviction,” it dwells on her commitment to craftsmanship. The scrapbook-style spreads showcase mock-ups of her early brainstorming, the fabrics she insisted on, the dovetailed furniture joints and delicate details on all those teeny accessories that girls craved and parents put on their credit cards. Designed as a nostalgia trip for Millennials, it works. My 9- and 4-year-old daughters showed the book off to their playmates one weekend afternoon, but it was those girls’ 40-something mom who lingered over it with me, comparing notes on the expensive items we had known better than to ask for in childhood, such as the bisque plate and mug for Kirsten, made by the renowned Rowe Pottery Works in Wisconsin. But what about the rest of the story of the doll that had become America’s second-most-popular by the late ’90s? That’s left to Amanda FitzSimons, a journalist who did not have the cooperation of Mattel, or of the now-85-year-old Rowland, for her smart and colorful cultural analysis, An American Girl: How a Billion-Dollar Doll and Its Unlikely Founder Changed Girlhood Forever . That means she’s free, after exploring how the dolls and books became unexpected hits, to describe how the American Girl brand’s identity eventually grew so muddled that it has become barely recognizable. FitzSimons starts with Rowland’s big idea, conceived on a trip to Colonial Williamsburg in the early 1980s and transformed into an elaborate business plan over a weekend at her northern-Wisconsin cabin, where the woodstove and outhouse had her thinking about life in the past. The books, “for girls about girls,” came first—they were “the heart of” the American Girl collection, in Rowland’s words. A boss who looked for tenacity in her employees as well as her dolls, Rowland liked to say that her initials, PTR, stood for “Prepare to Redo”; a researcher at the company devoted a day, for example, to conferring with poultry-science experts to determine the exact hour at which Kirsten’s hens would lay eggs. With that attention to detail, Rowland turned the business into a high-volume, high-value sensation. Over time, Pleasant Company offered ever more accessories, such as carefully constructed craft kits (I had my eye on a wooden loom for weaving a doll sash), stationery, and matching outfits for dolls and their girls. But above all, what Rowland sold was the idea that girlhood was important, in need of preservation. Her American Girl enterprise, FitzSimons argues, was a mission to rescue an endangered phase of life. Girlhood was slipping away. The term tween , which encompasses kids as young as 8, was popularized as a marketing tool in the ’80s and quickly became shorthand for a child who didn’t act like a child. Late-20th-century girls, Rowland worried from the start, “turn on the television set and the world comes down on them hard. It’s sexually explicit, it’s dangerous and violent, it’s angry, complaining, discouraging.” By the mid-’90s, the phenomenon of kids aging out of pastimes earlier was well documented. FitzSimons credits Rowland with an astute insight amid rising calls to shore up girls’ self-confidence: “It wasn’t that girls wanted to be older,” she writes; “it was that they wanted to be understood, feel important.” The dolls’ figures never matured, and the books didn’t include periods or crushes; friends, school, and adventure occupied the girls’ imaginations. Samantha fights back when a local menace puts salt in her birthday ice cream; colonial-era Felicity Merriman befriends the daughter of a Loyalist family despite her father’s Revolutionary politics. In aiming to transport girls to other worlds, Rowland had more than innocent fantasy and vivid Americana in mind. Her goal was to encourage play that felt immersive and incorporated historical adversity . The books included plotlines about children working in factories and the displacement of Native people in the Midwest. Her cast expanded to include a second trio of dolls—Felicity, as well as Josefina Montoya , who lives on a New Mexico rancho in 1824, and Addy Walker , an enslaved girl who escapes to 1864 Philadelphia. Elizabeth Renstrom for The Atlantic Josefina Elizabeth Renstrom for The Atlantic Addy The panels of scholars hired to help vet the dolls’ backgrounds and physical appearance had their socially charged work cut out for them. Lonnie Bunch, later the founding director of the National Museum of African American History and Culture, was part of the committee advising on Addy, whose development stirred plenty of debate over her storyline (whether American Girl’s only Black doll should have been born into slavery, for example) and over specifics (which hair texture was appropriate, how cheerful faces should look in book illustrations). People argued about her suitability as a possession for white girls. (Endorsed by Oprah in time for Christmas 1993, Addy was a commercial success that year.) [ Read: American Girls aren’t radical anymore ] The original six American Girls telegraphed a spirit of optimism about the very idea of being a girl. Rowland’s characters were intrepid and resourceful but still gracious; free to be tomboyish while also engaged with feminine traditions, such as Kirsten’s quilting. Breaking down gender stereotypes wasn’t Rowland’s goal, and “feminism was never mentioned in the room,” the creative director of American Girl magazine told FitzSimons. But the “girls can do anything” spirit of third-wave feminism, cresting in the ’90s, was the backdrop of the brand’s rise: empowerment and education in one finely crafted package. As Rowland put it in a letter addressed to parents in an early catalog, “Growing up in America is, has been, and can always be an experience to treasure.” “I don’t care if a girl grew up in Colonial times, Victorian times, in 1950, or today,” Rowland once said. “The emotional experiences of childhood are absolutely true and constant.” Thanks in part to my own exposure to her dolls’ stories, I confess I can’t quite believe that she ever really meant this. The hardships entailed in Kirsten’s months-long sea voyage stunned snack-happy 8-year-old me; I was suddenly aware of the many conveniences and freedoms that I took for granted. Our kinship was strong—we even shared a birthday (June 8)—but our attachment, I felt, was also about imagining how different my days and moods were from hers. When Rowland sold her venture (for $700 million), the business was just expanding into American Girl stores and cafés, an old-fashioned “mecca,” she called it, for mother-daughter doll bonding (and buying). The world’s virtual horizons had barely begun to be mapped, and the looming kids-getting-older-younger landscape was soon Mattel’s problem to worry about. Over the past two decades, according to one study, the average age at which children begin to be interested in “adult-oriented topics such as fashion and technology” has decreased from age 12 to 8. In 1990, little girls were hoping for $50 nightgowns to match the one their doll wore; now they’re pining for $90 Drunk Elephant glycolic serum to slather on their faces before bed. For Mattel at the turn of the millennium, adultified competition arrived in an unnervingly direct and provocative form: Bratz dolls, aimed at young girls. With their pillowy lips, heavy eye makeup, and distorted big-head-small-body proportions, they were mutant Barbies, accelerants for the idea that brasher and sexier were better. By 2006, they accounted for 40 percent of the fashion-doll market. The American Girl heritage was buried as Mattel played catch-up. Except for Addy and Josefina, the original dolls were retired. Catalogs shrank; chic burgundy gave way to hot pink. Proliferating doll lines—Best Friends, Truly Me, WellieWishers—shifted the focus away from the bond between a girl and her doll, as a New Yorker article noted, and onto friendship networks. Instead of intriguing relics from earlier times—a miniature oil lamp or a friendship quilt—the Girl of the Year doll (the run is limited, so buy her fast) had plastic-tchotchke versions of things such as a cellphone and a Stanley-style water bottle. New dolls that were added to the historical American Girl line soon hailed from more recent times; Courtney Moore, who “never met a mixtape she didn’t like,” was from 1986, the year the brand was launched. The accompanying books became perfunctory, a scattershot array of graphics and a story that gestured at history but never dove in. Even as doll prices rose, American Girl revenue cratered, reportedly falling by 61 percent from 2016 to late 2023. In a recent Instagram post, a mom vented about a visit to the books section at an American Girl store: “Excuse me. Where are the boxed sets. Where are the SACRED TEXTS. The Library of Alexandria, again.” Mattel notably hasn’t bothered to reissue the full book series, though the six original dolls have been rereleased for the brand’s anniversary. Instead, targeting its Millennial fan base, the company commissioned a new book in the Samantha series from the best-selling historical novelist Fiona Davis, whose other work for adults features adventurous young women in glamorous and gritty 20th-century New York City. Elizabeth Renstrom for The Atlantic A Modern Era Kirsten doll, now with space buns and an updated dress, and the six original American Girl dolls In Samantha: The Next Chapter , Davis locates her subject in 1920. Now 25, Samantha is down on her luck in New York (her family’s fortune has been stolen) and working as a shopgirl. But she soon finds the thieves and helps the suffragists’ cause, championed by her Aunt Cornelia in the original books. For some readers, Davis’s aim of evoking “sweet nostalgia” and inspiring “wonder at the women you’ve become,” as she has put it, may prove rewarding. Yet her American Girl audience is ambivalent, too. Reared on Rowland’s vision of boldly imaginative girls eager to play their part in an America that was constantly improving, Millennials are also dealing with disenchantment: The country they now inhabit hasn’t delivered on the optimism that powered the world of the dolls and books they loved. Davis’s grown-up Samantha, though a tribute to the brand’s history-infused approach, is likely to disappoint. She is stuffed with generically desirable attributes of womanhood and faces conventional emotional dilemmas: She’s determined to remain independent while looking for love, forward-thinking yet happy with her lot. It’s a formula for tame likability rather than conflicted maturity. Earlier this year, the latest American Girl catalog landed on my doorstep—it was a re-creation of the first catalog cover, which showed a girl curled up with her doll on a chintz-covered window seat, intently reading a book. But inside, after a few pages dedicated to the historical dolls, was a torrent of brand collaborations (with Hill House Home dresses, Disney princesses, Polly Pocket) and a spread welcoming the Modern Era collection—the classic dolls, now offered in shrunken, all-vinyl versions with oversize heads, and dressed up in trendy contemporary outfits. American Girl has a tough needle to thread (the cliché seems apt): make the dolls of good quality, but not too costly; repackage American history, but don’t offend anyone; get Gen Alpha girls interested, but remember that Millennials now hold the credit cards. I’ve deemed my 4-year-old too young for a $175 doll, and my Harry Potter –obsessed 9-year-old considers my vintage Kirsten books too slender to take seriously. But when an old 1995 catalog I’d ordered for research arrived, both pored over it, fascinated by Samantha’s miniature brass lunch pail and Felicity’s coal bed warmer. I explained that the company no longer makes those items; we can get them only for astronomical sums on resale sites. “But this is all so perfect,” my elder daughter said. “It almost makes them come alive.” This article appears in the December 2026 print edition with the headline “Kirsten’s Midlife Crisis.”

items.title: AVAS 2026: Accra to drive Africa’s Tokenisation Agenda
items.description: Ghana will host the Africa Virtual Asset Summit (AVAS) on November 2–3, 2026, as the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Ghana, convenes regulators, policymakers and industry leaders to advance a trusted, inclusive and innovative virtual asset ecosystem across Africa. The summit, taking place at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City, Accra, will be held under the theme, “Tokenisation: Africa’s Pathway Towards Building a Trusted, Inclusive and Innovative Virtual Asset Ecosystem.” At the heart of the gathering is the proposed Accra Declaration, a shared set of principles and recommendations intended to guide the responsible development of virtual assets and tokenisation across the continent. Tokenisation—the digital representation of assets—offers opportunities to unlock value in gold, real estate, cocoa, bonds and trade receivables, potentially widening access to investment and improving the way assets are owned, transferred and traded. Ghana is already exploring these opportunities through its regulatory sandbox, including applications involving gold and Treasury bills. AVAS 2026 aims to move the conversation beyond possibilities towards practical outcomes, including policy recommendations, stronger dialogue between regulators and market participants, and cross-border partnerships to support responsible innovation. The summit is expected to bring together securities regulators, central banks, finance ministries, financial intelligence units, stock exchanges, banks, asset managers, pension funds, insurers, virtual asset service providers, fintech companies, investors, legal practitioners, academics and development partners. Among the announced keynote speakers are Finance Minister Hon. Dr. Cassiel Ato Baah Forson; Governor of the Bank of Ghana, Dr. Johnson Pandit Asiama; SEC Director-General Dr. James Klutse Avedzi; Chief of Staff Hon. Julius Debrah; and Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Hon. Samuel Nartey George. The proposed Accra Declaration will be central to the summit’s ambition to establish common ground for responsible tokenisation, encourage cooperation among jurisdictions and support the development of credible virtual asset markets. As African economies explore new ways to mobilise capital and expand financial inclusion, AVAS 2026 will provide a platform for shaping the policies and partnerships needed to realise tokenisation’s potential. The event is presented with the involvement of the Securities and Exchange Commission, Ghana. Registration information is available at www.avas2026.com .

items.title: Faranah : colère des étudiants après le décès tragique de leur camarade
items.description: Un étudiant a tragiquement perdu la vie lors d’un match de football à Faranah, dans la soirée de ce mardi 28 octobre 2026. Ses camarades pointent du doigt l'hôpital régional. ​La victime est Morlaye Clavère Maouomou, étudiant en première année de licence (L1) au département d’économie rurale, filière gestion des entreprises agricoles. ​Selon un communiqué de l’institution : « Le drame est survenu dans la soirée du mardi 27 octobre 2026. Le jeune étudiant se trouvait sur un terrain de sport lorsqu'il a été victime d'une crise cardiaque foudroyante. » ​Suite à ce décès, des tensions ont éclaté aux alentours de l’hôpital régional de Faranah. Plusieurs étudiants ont vivement mis en cause le personnel médical, l'accusant d'avoir tardé à prendre en charge leur camarade, faute du paiement préalable d'une somme de 30 000 GNF. ​« Quand il a fait la crise, nous l'avons transporté à l'hôpital. Sur place, ils ont commencé à nous poser des questions d'argent, et notre ami a rendu l'âme pendant ce temps », a témoigné un étudiant présent sur les lieux. ​ ​Contacté par Guineenews, le directeur de l'hôpital regional, Dr Ibrahim Nabé, a déclaré ceci : « Le jeune jouait au football dans le quartier, c’est là où il a eu un arrêt cardiaque. Ses amis l’ont pris pour l’emmener à l’hôpital. Malheureusement, nous avons reçu un dépôt de corps, c’est-à-dire qu’il n’est pas arrivé vivant dans notre structure. » ​Au sein du campus de l'ISAV, règnent tristesse et consternation à la suite de cette disparition brutale.

items.title: Constitutional reform must deliver institutions that serve Ghanaians
items.description: A judge may be independent on paper and still struggle to deliver justice because a court lacks staff, reliable computers or funds to operate. A public institution may have impressive legal powers yet depend on political goodwill for appointments and resources. These contradictions should be central to Ghana’s constitutional reform debate. The question is practical: how do we build institutions that serve citizens fairly, whichever party governs? The judiciary provides a useful example. Courts interpret laws, settle disputes and check abuses of executive and legislative power. Their effectiveness affects everyone, from a trader pursuing an unpaid debt to a family contesting land ownership. When cases drag on, businesses lose money, relationships deteriorate and confidence in lawful solutions weakens. Independence needs resources “Even judges must eat” captures an important truth. Judges and court workers need decent conditions, while courts need buildings, records, equipment and functioning systems. Independence requires the means to do the work. Ghana’s Constitution already recognises this. Article 127 protects judicial independence, including financial administration. It charges judicial administrative expenses on the Consolidated Fund, protects conditions of service and requires quarterly releases of judicial funds. The Judicial Service Act, 2020, also provides for administration, funding, audit and reporting. The challenge is making these protections work. Citizens should be able to see what courts request, what Parliament approves, what is released and how the money is spent. Institutions receiving public funds must explain both their needs and their results. A 1988 study published by the Centre for the Independence of Judges and Lawyers makes a distinction that remains useful: freedom to decide cases must be supported by security in employment and material conditions. Constitutional promises lose value when inflation erodes salaries or funding commitments go unmet. Appointments must inspire confidence Under Article 144, Supreme Court appointments involve the President, Judicial Council, Council of State and Parliament. Sharing responsibility creates safeguards, but procedures must also inspire public confidence. In Ghana Bar Association and Others v Attorney-General and Others, decided in 2016, the Supreme Court confirmed that a Supreme Court appointment requires a Judicial Council recommendation, although the President need not appoint every recommended person. The Constitution Review Committee proposes more structured selection procedures. Government’s July 2026 Position Paper rejects the proposed constitutional changes to appointment processes, favouring existing arrangements. These differences deserve public debate. Published vacancies, clear criteria and transparent procedures would help citizens judge whether merit drives appointments. Britain’s Constitutional Reform Act 2005 established a Judicial Appointments Commission, operating from 2006 principally in England and Wales. Ghana need not copy it, but can learn from its emphasis on merit and good character. Protection must reach Circuit and District Courts too. Existing constitutional safeguards should be acknowledged, while staffing, working conditions and disciplinary procedures receive serious attention. Most citizens experience justice through these courts. Social pressure matters Political interference is only part of the problem. Public officials also face demands from relatives, friends, schoolmates, religious communities and party supporters. Requests for preferential treatment often arrive as appeals to loyalty or gratitude. My 2008 doctoral research at Oxford Brookes University examined cultural and institutional pressures through surveys and 35 interviews. Discussing approaches to judges on behalf of relatives, participant PA2 argued: “He should be cut off from such things so that when he goes he reads the case and gives objective judgements.” This illustrates perceived pressure from personal connections; it does not establish that all judges yield to it. Family solidarity is valuable. So are funerals, weddings and community celebrations. However, expectations of lavish spending and reciprocal favours can place pressure on public workers. Better salaries help, but cannot replace ethical boundaries. Articles 284 and 286 already address conflicts of interest and asset declarations. Enforcement matters. Public office should never become a means of financing social status or rewarding personal networks. Respect for authority should allow questioning. Community loyalty should coexist with impartiality. Our cultural strengths include investment in children’s education and mutual support; reform should build on these while challenging practices that undermine fairness. Technology should improve justice Digital reform deserves sustained investment. Electronic filing, searchable records, digital payments and reliable hearing schedules could reduce missing files, unnecessary journeys and opportunities for unofficial payments. Case management systems should record adjournments and their reasons, helping judges identify avoidable delays. Appropriate remote hearings could save time without weakening fair participation. Citizens should be able to track cases and obtain published judgments. Public reporting should show case age, vacancies, expenditure and performance. However, judges should not be pressured to sacrifice careful decisions merely to improve disposal figures. Technology also needs maintenance, training, cybersecurity and proper judicial control. People without internet access or digital skills must receive assistance. A computer system that excludes citizens cannot deliver accessible justice. Reform must also address political financing. When financial support for parties is treated as an investment to be repaid through appointments, contracts or access, public institutions become vulnerable to private interests. Transparent financing and credible scrutiny can help interrupt that cycle. A shared national responsibility Afrobarometer’s 2024 survey found that only 35% of Ghanaians trusted courts somewhat or a lot, compared with 57% in 2017. Such perceptions underline the need to rebuild confidence through visible fairness and accountability. Citizens, journalists and professional bodies have responsibilities too. They should scrutinise decisions, demand reliable information and challenge wrongdoing without assuming every unpopular judgment reflects corruption. Protecting legitimate authority and questioning its use are compatible democratic duties. The CRC’s recommendations emerged from nationwide consultation. Government’s position is an executive response, not the end of the conversation. Where proposals differ, citizens deserve clear explanations and genuine efforts to find agreement. Ghana needs transparent appointments, predictable funding, stronger oversight, effective ethical enforcement and technology that improves services. Some changes require constitutional amendment; others require legislation or implementation of safeguards already in place. It behoves all well-meaning Ghanaians to help secure agreement on necessary reforms and hold authorities accountable for delivery. Constitutional reform must become a shared national responsibility that survives changes of government. Institutions should belong to the Republic. Their authority must serve all citizens fairly, their resources must match their responsibilities, and their independence must be accompanied by accountability.

items.title: Netanyahu gana las elecciones en Israel, pero su coalición no logra la mayoría
items.description: El partido de Benjamín Netanyahu, el Likud, ha ganado las elecciones legislativas celebradas el martes en Israel . El primer ministro no lograría, sin embargo, ni siquiera con los apoyos de sus aliados ultranacionalistas y religiosos, la mayoría de escaños del Parlamento (61) necesaria para seguir gobernando. Una vez escrutado más del 70% de los votos, el partido del jefe de Gobierno israelí obtiene en torno a 27 diputados sobre un total de 120. El partido Yashar (centroderecha), de su adversario, Gadi Eisenkot , sumaría 22, menos de lo que vaticinaban las encuestas previas a estos comicios, que lo situaban como primera fuerza. Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa Troops of Operation Enduring Peace, OPEP, have arrested two suspects over an alleged attack on members of a vigilante group and the subsequent burning of their office in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The suspects were arrested at about 1:40 a.m. on October 27, 2026, in the NEPA area of Jos North. Media Information Officer of OPEP, Capt. Chinonso Polycarp Oteh, who confirmed the arrests, said the suspects were apprehended by troops of Sector 1, OPEP. Oteh said, “The arrest followed allegations linking the suspects to the attack on vigilante personnel and the subsequent setting ablaze of their office.” He said, “The suspects are currently in custody for further investigation and necessary action.” Oteh said, “The arrests form part of ongoing efforts by OPEP to tackle criminal activities and maintain peace across Plateau State.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” ” We call on members of the public to cooperate with the military and other security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing criminal activities and apprehending suspects.” Oteh said, “The continued cooperation and support of members of the public remain crucial to our efforts to maintain peace and security across the state.” He added, “Security personnel will continue to intensify operations aimed at identifying and apprehending individuals involved in acts capable of undermining peace and security in the state.” The post Military arrests two over attack on vigilantes, burning of Jos office appeared first on Vanguard News .
